projects.title: Show HN: Muscle Memory – Can you still write code without AI?
projects.author: ekkuleivonen
projects.summary: Developer of 6 years here, been using AI (increasingly) over the last year for most of my work. A few weeks back I started to look for new jobs as the current startup I work for is falling into pieces. "Do I need to do leetcode again?" - I thought. So I picked a few challenges and tried to solve them without an assistant. This felt impossible. What?! Is this the brainrot everyone is talking about? I mean I still read code every day, I just don't write it anymore. I could read and review the solution easily, but writing it myself felt like speaking a language I only understand, but cannot speak. Being the data hoarder I am, I immediately wanted numbers, so I built Muscle Memory to help me feed them. It's like leetcode but better. Challenges are more realistic, and I'd like to think the UX is more straightforward. It covers 12 languages and your code runs in a network-denied sandbox in your browser. No account needed. I want it to be a place to keep your hands sharp: short tasks, clear prompts, and difficulty that comes from solving the problem rather than figuring out what the question means. About the data (that I'm curious about): With your consent, Muscle Memory records your practice as raw events, including keystrokes, runs and submissions. Hoping to build an open dataset of how we write code in the AI era. That could help us understand how we approach problems, where we get stuck, and how we well do we retain our craft during this transition. Your individual results stay private unless you share them. “Stealth” mode keeps your data out of published findings, and you can export or delete everything. The data will be published as a report/notebook on the site itself, and be available raw under MIT license (parquet) once we reach a critical mass of sorts, so it makes sense to share. The code is also MIT-licensed on GitHub (https://github.com/ekkuleivonen/muscle-memory). I wrote more about why I built it in the manifesto here: https://musclememory.run/manifesto. I'd especially like to hear what surprised you about your first attempt. Try it out here: https://musclememory.run

projects.title: Railse：一个人同时开几个 AI 编程 agent，审批推到手机上点一下
projects.author: Railse547
projects.summary: 最近几个月我一直同时开着 Claude Code 、Codex 和 Gemini CLI 写代码。agent 本身跑得挺好，烦的是它每次要跑命令、改文件都停下来等我按「允许」。三个终端轮流翻，经常翻到的时候它已经等了十分钟；出去吃个饭，回来每个都停在第一条 git push 上。开 yolo 全放行又不敢，一句 rm -rf 出去就没有后悔药。 所以我写了 Railse：每条审批先过一遍规则，规则定不了的推到手机，我在手机上点一下，agent 接着跑。 它怎么做： - 三家 CLI 的权限钩子都接到本机一个守护进程，规则只写一套。 - 每条请求先定风险档：只读和改项目里的文件直接放行； curl 、npm install 这类联网的，git push 、deploy 这类对外的，rm -rf 、git reset --hard 这类不可逆的，都问。 - 定不了的推到手机，Web Push 通知，点开批准或拒绝。批准时勾「记住」，当场存成规则，下次同类的不问。 - 对外和不可逆的永远不能被「记住」放行，只能自己手写规则。 - Railse 自己挂了不卡 agent：守护进程没起、hub 连不上超过 30 秒，CLI 弹自己的审批框，最坏就是回到没装的样子。 hub 自己部署，一个 Go 二进制，也有 Fly.io 的现成配置；手机网页由 hub 托管，不用另外部署。命令里认得出的 token 、密码在本机就换成 再上报。 现状：v0.1.2 ，我自己在用。已知的限制：Gemini CLI 的钩子只能拒绝不能放行； Codex 的钩子只在交互会话里生效； iPhone 要加到主屏幕才能收推送； hub 是单机 SQLite 。 开源，Apache 2.0： https://github.com/xufei547/railse-opc 一行安装：curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xufei547/railse-opc/main/install.sh | sh 想听两种反馈：你同时开几个 agent 的时候是怎么处理审批的；规则表有判错的（该放行的问了、该问的放行了）直接提 issue ，我会优先看。

projects.title: 用 Web Components 做了个全栈框架 Gemkit，首屏 JS 26KB， SSR 性能和 SvelteKit 差不多
projects.author: 594mantou
projects.summary: 几年前在这发过我写的 Web Components 库 Gem （ https://v2ex.com/t/738230 ），一直有个硬伤：只有客户端渲染。连它自带的文档站生成器 gem-book 也是 CSR ，搜索引擎基本收录不到啥东西。 之前在这问过 React SSR 和自定义元素怎么配合（ https://v2ex.com/t/998353 ），当时我自己回复说「用 jsdom 模拟生成 ShadowDOM 理论上也行」。后来真这么干了： 1. 先用 jsdom 做原型，跑通了序列化（输出 Declarative Shadow DOM ）和水合（复用服务端的 DOM ，不重建） 2. 再把 jsdom 去掉，直接渲染成字符串，用 AsyncLocalStorage 做请求隔离，支持流式输出，这就是 gem-ssr 3. 最近参考 Next.js 和 SvelteKit ，在 gem-ssr 上做了应用框架 Gemkit ## 长啥样 一个文件就是一个页面： ```ts // src/pages/blog/[slug].ts @page ({ load: ({ params }) => getPost(params.slug), title: ({ data }) => data.title, }) export default class PostPage extends GemElement { @property data?: Post; @template() #content = () => html` ${this.data?.title} `; } ``` 只在服务端跑的代码放同名的 `[slug].server.ts` ，可以读 cookie 、redirect 、处理表单 actions ，不会打包到客户端。用过 SvelteKit 的应该很熟悉。 其他能力： - 文件路由、嵌套布局、i18n - 默认 SSG ，部署静态托管就行；需要的页面可以按请求渲染，也支持 ISR - `@server()` 元素只在服务端渲染，代码和依赖不进客户端；`@lazy()` 元素用户交互时才加载代码水合，第一次点击不会丢 - 本身就是个 Rsbuild 插件，Rsbuild 的东西照常用 - 内置 Vercel / Netlify / Cloudflare 适配 ## 和其他框架比了下 用 RealWorld （ Medium 克隆）各实现了一遍，同一个后端、同一份数据： | | 首页 JS (gzip) | Lighthouse | FCP | SSR req/s | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Gemkit | 25.9 KB | 100 | 906 ms | 1382 | | SvelteKit | 44.0 KB | 100 | 1285 ms | 1437 | | Nuxt | 85.8 KB | 99 | 1656 ms | 1042 | | Next.js | 103.5 KB | 96 | 908 ms | 317 | SSR 吞吐 SvelteKit 略高一点，两个其实都快到后端的上限了。测试代码、复现步骤和原始数据都在这： https://github.com/mantou132/realworld/tree/framework-comparison/frameworks ，觉得测得不对的欢迎指出来。 ## 不足 - 个人项目，还是 0.x ，没在大项目里用过 - 客户端导航是先改 URL 再渲染新页面，加载期间会看到新 URL + 旧页面，后面再改 ## 试试 ```sh npm create gemkit@latest my-app ``` - 文档： https://gemkit.gemjs.org/zh - 仓库： https://github.com/mantou132/gem - 完整的过程写了篇文章（英文）： https://dev.to/mantou132/from-client-only-to-ssr-building-gemkit-a-sveltekit-style-framework-for-web-components-8ag 欢迎拍砖，觉得有意思的话点个 star 吧。

projects.summary: OpenMathpix 是一款把公式截图转为 LaTeX 的桌面工具，适合写论文、整理数学笔记和制作课件。集成 Pix2Text MFR-1.5，首次下载模型后即可在 CPU 上离线识别，无需 Python、显卡或 API 账号。支持快捷截图、图片粘贴与拖入、公式预览、复制及历史记录，提供 Windows 便携版。 亮点 作者自荐。希望让日常写论文、整理数学笔记时的公式录入更方便。 本地公式识别：集成 Pix2Text MFR-1.5，首次下载约 120 MB 模型后即可离线运行。本地模式下截图在本机 CPU 上处理，无需部署 Python、GPU 或大语言模型服务。 完整的桌面使用流程：支持快捷键截图、粘贴与拖入图片；识别后可预览公式、复制 LaTeX，并在历史记录中重新查看。 可直接试用：提供 Windows x64 便携 EXE 和中英文使用说明，模型下载带进度、完整性校验及修复入口。 识别引擎可选：保留 PaddleOCR API 配置入口，可按需使用云端或自托管服务处理文字、表格及文档版面。 实现可供学习：使用 Electron、TypeScript 和 ONNX Runtime，将专用视觉模型推理放在独立后台进程中，附有测试和可复现的公式样例。 本地 MFR 引擎主要用于单个公式截图；识别模型来自 Pix2Text，本项目侧重桌面截图、推理接入与结果管理。 试用入口： Windows 便携版下载 中文使用说明 启动应用后，在 Settings 中选择 Local MFR-1.5，点击 Download MFR-1.5 下载模型，再点击 Save & Test Local Model。Windows 本地推理需要 Microsoft Visual C++ x64 运行库。

projects.title: Show HN: Crulon – Business phone where AI does the work, humans make the calls
projects.author: rayn11
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Rayhan. Crulon is a business phone system where an AI agent answers the line and your team works alongside it. You can talk with our demo agent right in your browser, no sign-up: https://crulon.ai/#talk Why I built it: I’ve spent eight years as a software and network engineer, mostly building tools for internet providers, and kept watching small support teams lose customers in the seams. Calls missed after hours. Calls passed from a bot to a person who had to start over. Most voice AI products are a bot sitting on someone else’s phone line, so a handoff means forwarding to another number and losing the context. We built the phone system and the agent as one thing. What that gets you: The handoff happens inside the same system. When something isn’t the AI’s job, it asks the caller, then rings your team (in the browser or on a desk phone) with a note on why they’re calling. Live calls: anyone with permission can listen to an AI call (no one on the call can hear them) and take it over. It’s the same call, with no transfer and no hold music; the AI just leaves. Tools: the agent can call any API you define in an Action builder (look up the caller, open a ticket), and it checks with the caller before changing anything. Outbound campaigns: the agent works through a call list for reminders, renewals and follow-ups, and puts interested people through to your team. SIP desk phones, and bring-your-own-carrier so you can keep your numbers. If you run out of AI minutes, calls follow your fallback route (ring the team, voicemail) instead of dropping, and the refused call isn’t billed. How it’s built, briefly: calls come in over SIP into Call Flows (menus, queues, schedules), and your team answers in the browser or on SIP desk phones. Each agent runs on one of two engines. Classic transcribes, thinks, then speaks, so you get exact wording and English, Spanish and French. Live is a full-duplex speech model that listens while it talks and hands tool work to a second model. One fun problem with that split was teaching the agent when to hang up, which I wrote up here: https://crulon.ai/blog/teaching-a-voice-agent-to-hang-up It isn’t a CRM; it works alongside yours. Built-in Apps connect it to systems like billing and network tools, and anything with a web API plugs in through the Action builder. Pricing is per seat ($24, $49 or $89 a month) with a pool of AI minutes; human calls are included. If you sign up this month, HN30 takes 30% off the first 3 months. I’ll be here all day. Try the agent, try to trip it up, and tell me what you’d want from a phone system like this.

projects.title: Show HN: Sectr – Serverless backend platform for easy deployment of AI agents
projects.author: donald_pinckney
projects.summary: Hey HN, I've been building Sectr, a backend-as-a-service for making it easy(ier) to develop and deploy AI agents. Deploying agents requires non-trivial systems design work. Consider a support agent: how do you stream messages to your frontend, how/where do you persist messages for frontend fetching later (or for auditing), and when the agent wants to issue a refund, do you spin-down the compute infra while it's waiting on human approval? Sectr aims to be the serverless abstraction and platform to provide these systems for you. No sign-up needed to try using the dev server: curl -fsSL https://sectr.dev/install.sh | sh # Install CLI sectr init my-agent && cd my-agent # Starter code sectr dev # Dev server, with UI to test chatting Sectr provides: - Streaming of every token, tool call and event, and persistence so they can be loaded fresh later. - Scaling up, and down to zero when the agent needs to wait, and resumption right to the suspended agent's state. - Human approved tools automatically use Sectr's suspension and resumption capabilities, no code needed from you. - AG-UI endpoint for any deployed agent so you can trivially hook up your frontend - Local dev server experience, so you can rapidly debug and iterate on your agent's behavior At the core, you can deploy any container image to Sectr as long as it implements a certain shaped HTTP endpoint. In practice, currently Sectr provides adapters to let you deploy your existing OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, or Pydantic AI agents, with only 2 new lines of code: app = AgentApp(name="support") app.add_route("/chat", openai_agents(agent)) Certainly the hardest part of building Sectr was getting the resumption logic to be correct and invisible, across the Program State x Model Provider x Agent Framework matrix. For example, an earlier bug was when a model replied with text plus a tool call, Sectr would resume that as two separate messages, instead of one message with a text and tool part. This works, but breaks prompt caching (and might subtly change model behavior). Sectr is free during the beta (and can be tried locally without sign-up); I mainly want feedback, especially on dev & deployment experiences, any bugs, and what features would excite you. Introductory video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H-y3wynkKc0 Docs: https://docs.sectr.dev

projects.author: wisteen
projects.summary: 做 iOS app 的应该都遇到过：从浏览器复制的 App Store 链接带国家代码，比如 `apps.apple.com/us/app/...`。发给其他国家的人，要么进的是美区页面，要么 app 在他那个区没上架，直接提示这个 App 在你所在的国家或地区不可用。 所以写了个小工具 Hither： https://hither.link/ 用法：粘贴任意国家的 App Store 链接或者 app ID ，得到 `hither.link/ `。 每次点击时： - Cloudflare Worker 从请求里读访客所在国家（`request.cf.country`） - 调 Apple 公开的 lookup 接口（`itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=...&country=...`）查这个区有没有上架，结果在边缘缓存一天 - 有上架：跳到访客自己国家的商店页面 - 没上架：先试美区，再按英国、加拿大、澳洲、德国、日本等大区依次找，找到有上架的为止 踩到的一个坑：iPhone / iPad 上 App Store app 只能打开当前账号所在国家的商店，跳到外区链接一样会提示不可用。所以 iOS 访客看到的是一个小页面，有 app 图标、名字和一个跳到有上架商店的按钮；电脑和安卓直接跳转。 其他： - 不用注册，没有数据库。链接里只有 app ID ，所以不会过期，也没人能改它跳去哪 - 上架前就能生成链接：用 App Store Connect 里 App 信息页的 Apple ID - 商店信息缓存最多一天，新上架的区可能要等一下才识别到 代码 MIT 开源，跑在 Cloudflare 免费套餐上，想自己部署一份也很快： https://github.com/wisteenio/hither 接下来在考虑 Google Play 链接、自定义短名、二维码，大家觉得哪个更有用？也欢迎提我没想到的边界情况。

projects.title: Show HN: Limma – MCP for total recall and precision in data retrieval for agents
projects.author: BerendG
projects.summary: Hello, my name is Berend Graham. My cofounder Shiv Oberai and I have been working on Limma for a year now with the goal of building a proactive solution to the reliability issues that plague practical AI and agentic use in companies with RAG. Limma is a single MCP that exists for the sole purpose of ensuring that the right information is retrieved with every query and no information is skipped and or missed. This means total precision and recall. We've found that this approach leads to the lowest rate of hallucination vs. solely targeting agent action verification which has made tremendous strides in capability. We do this by building a map and structuring all data-points within unstructured data as well as federating structured data for addressability so that agents don't need to search through chunks directly and instead only get the right information . We wanted this to be extremely easy to use so that anyone can set it up and try it within minutes so that the precision issues (especially with large quantities of data) that LLMs struggle with can finally be remedied. We use self-hosted models (primarily Qwen models as of current) so that the system can be deployed on one's own server if needed, and also to optimize for speed. We have a free monthly version on our website if anyone would like to try it out and provide feedback!

projects.summary: # Space.Map — 让每一字节，都一目了然 **Space.Map** 是一款基于 .NET 10 和 WPF 构建的现代化 Windows 磁盘空间可视化分析工具，致力于让复杂的磁盘空间管理变得简单、直观且高效。 你是否曾遇到磁盘空间莫名不足，却不知道哪些文件占用了大量容量？Space.Map 正是为解决这一问题而生。 通过直观的 **Treemap（矩形树图）可视化技术**，Space.Map 将传统的文件目录结构转化为色彩鲜明、大小分明的交互式图形，让磁盘空间分布一目了然，帮助用户快速定位大文件、分析存储占用，告别繁琐的文件夹逐级排查。 ### ✨ 核心亮点 - **直观的空间可视化**：通过 Squarified Treemap 算法，以矩形面积呈现文件和文件夹的空间占用情况。 - **高效的磁盘扫描**：采用迭代式 DFS 遍历与渐进式扫描机制，持续反馈扫描结果。 - **快速定位大文件**：自动统计占用空间最大的 100 个文件，轻松发现存储空间的主要消耗来源。 - **交互式目录探索**：支持目录层级下钻和面包屑导航，自由探索文件结构。 - **现代化 Windows 界面**：采用 Fluent Design 设计语言，支持深色与浅色主题。 - **安全可靠的扫描机制**：针对深层目录、符号链接及重解析点进行防护，避免遍历异常和循环扫描。 - **中英文双语支持**：提供简体中文与英文界面，满足不同用户的使用需求。 ### 🚀 技术特色 项目基于 **C#、.NET 10、WPF 与 WPF-UI** 开发，采用模块化架构，将核心扫描算法、基础设施与界面展示清晰分离，兼顾性能、可维护性和可扩展性。 ### 🌍 开源理念 Space.Map 以 MIT 协议开源，欢迎开发者学习、交流、提出建议并参与贡献。 **让存储空间不再是冰冷的数字，而是一张可以自由探索的地图。** **Space.Map — See Where Every Byte Goes.** GitHub：https://github.com/ziyuhaokun/space-map

projects.title: Show HN: Open Dataset of the Lebanese Law
projects.author: nizarmah
projects.summary: Hey folks! I made it easier for builders to use the lebanese legislation through: a public DB, API, and MCP. The Lebanese University has an archive of all laws dating back to 1904 (legallaw.ul.edu.lb). People and AI can barely find it and navigate it. It also had outdated articles. Now, more people are using it. Builders for their startups, lawyers for their work, and students for their bar prep. I'm still trying to get it trusted by authorities. The database includes the edges between every law, article, ruling and Gazette issue. You can easily identify how they influence one another. Articles are versioned, so you can see how it was affected by other laws from the date it was published. 100k unofficial english translations were added using LLMs. They aren't accurate, but they help with search and SEO/AEO/GEO. We're working on producing legally accurate translations. 47k rulings were PDFs, some handwritten. We converted all of them to text using OCR, flagging handwritten files. We're working on an HTR model specifically for those to increase the confidence. Today, other datasets in Lebanon charge for this data. I'm doing it as a public service. I want change in my country. And, lately, I think it's through helping builders. Yet, what I'm doing is legally wrong, but hopefully morally acceptable.

projects.author: zwad3
projects.summary: Cryo is a programming language that models long-running tasks like workflows or AI agents. Programs freeze to disk when idle and can be thawed when new data arrives. As part of our announcement of Endothermic Labs, we've put together a small demo of Cryo that highlights its features and walks through the language and its plugin system. We originally built it as a way to deploy healthcare agents at scale, but have rebuilt it from the ground up to be a standalone toolchain for long-running tasks. It acts as something like a cross between Durable Objects and Temporal workflows, where the script itself is the durable unit with no replay needed. Cryo is statically and structurally typed, with a concurrency model similar to Go. It's still under active development, so we're holding off on open sourcing it until we're confident that the language is stable, ideally in the next 3-4 weeks.

projects.title: Show HN: Mainplane – Agent in Go that lives on your old PC, drives your laptop
projects.author: Alexander9
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Alexander. Yes, this is another agent harness. Here is why I built one anyway. I was engineer #2 at Browser Use, where I built our agent harness and the evals behind it, including BU Bench, which became a default benchmark for browser agents. I left in September to build Mainplane. The problem: local agents die with your laptop, and cloud agents can't reach your work. Many cloud platforms ask you to "select a repository", but my work is not that simple. I work across a desktop, a Mac mini and a laptop, and much of it is not in git. So I loaded Ubuntu on my old 2012 desktop and made it my Mainplane server. It has run for four weeks at a load average of 0.02, because the agents' tools run on other machines. How it works: it is a control plane architecture. The server runs the harness. It holds your API keys and every session, makes the LLM calls, and routes each tool call to a worker. The workers are your other machines, connected over a built-in private WireGuard network. A bash command runs in the worker's terminal, not on the server. Shared drives let projects move across machines. The agent works on your machines just like you would, but its state lives on the server, and your keys never leave it. Some design choices: - Every session is one append-only file. This is the agent state, and it is easily readable. If something breaks, you can resume it from the file. Observability comes for free: agent traces are just these state files. - Small by design. The system prompt is 3k tokens, and there are just two kinds of tools: shell and file (read, write, edit). At Browser Use, I learned the bitter lesson and found frontier models did better when I deleted all our helper functions. So I made the same bet here: bash is all you need. - No compaction. When a session fills up, /continue starts a new one that greps the previous state file, retrieving the context it needs, instead of reading a lossy summary. A /compact on a 400k-token session takes a while to write its summary. A /continue into a brand new session starts at once. - No permission prompts. A hyperintelligent misaligned agent WILL find a way around a permission system. The better strategy is giving the agent full unbounded access to a local computer, and only putting what you trust the agent with on that computer. - Why Go. WireGuard is written in Go, so the network compiles right into a 20 MB binary. Go is made for production servers, LLMs write it well, and the simplicity of Go matches how I like to build. Mainplane works with a Claude or ChatGPT subscription on the regular usage limits, or any API key. I would love your feedback, especially brutal and honest feedback and tasks that the harness cannot do. I'll be here all day to answer questions.

github.name: xxwioxx/hither
github.description: One App Store link for every country. Free, open-source Cloudflare Worker at hither.link.

projects.summary: 做 iOS app 的应该都遇到过：从浏览器复制的 App Store 链接带国家代码，比如 `apps.apple.com/us/app/...`。发给其他国家的人，要么进的是美区页面，要么 app 在他那个区没上架，直接提示这个 App 在你所在的国家或地区不可用。 所以写了个小工具 Hither： https://hither.link/ 用法：粘贴任意国家的 App Store 链接或者 app ID ，得到 `hither.link/ `。 每次点击时： - Cloudflare Worker 从请求里读访客所在国家（`request.cf.country`） - 调 Apple 公开的 lookup 接口（`itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=...&country=...`）查这个区有没有上架，结果在边缘缓存一天 - 有上架：跳到访客自己国家的商店页面 - 没上架：先试美区，再按英国、加拿大、澳洲、德国、日本等大区依次找，找到有上架的为止 踩到的一个坑：iPhone / iPad 上 App Store app 只能打开当前账号所在国家的商店，跳到外区链接一样会提示不可用。所以 iOS 访客看到的是一个小页面，有 app 图标、名字和一个跳到有上架商店的按钮；电脑和安卓直接跳转。 其他： - 不用注册，没有数据库。链接里只有 app ID ，所以不会过期，也没人能改它跳去哪 - 上架前就能生成链接：用 App Store Connect 里 App 信息页的 Apple ID - 商店信息缓存最多一天，新上架的区可能要等一下才识别到 代码 MIT 开源，跑在 Cloudflare 免费套餐上，想自己部署一份也很快： https://github.com/wisteenio/hither 接下来在考虑 Google Play 链接、自定义短名、二维码，大家觉得哪个更有用？也欢迎提我没想到的边界情况。

projects.title: Show HN: Hob - Open-source, on device alternative to Claude Cowork and ChatGPT
projects.author: pancomplex

github.name: FrigadeHQ/hob
github.description: An easier way to use AI on your own computer. A free, open-source alternative to Claude and ChatGPT that runs open-weight models like Gemma and gpt-oss locally on Mac, Windows and Linux. Private, and works offline.

projects.summary: Hey HN, I'm Christian and this is a new OSS project I've been noodling on for the last couple of weeks. Hob is a free, MIT-licensed desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux that works on your files the way the Claude and ChatGPT desktop apps do, except the model runs on your own computer. It uses open-weight models (currently Gemma 4 and gpt-oss). All your chats and files never leave your system. The only things that go online are web search (can be turned off in settings) and any MCP connectors you add yourself. Main features: - Automatically finds the best open-weight model for your hardware on first install (Mac/Linux/Windows) - Writes sandboxed Python code for ad hoc tools (data processing, document conversion, graphs etc.) - Built-in web search (powered by SearXNG) - MCP support - Image recognition - CRUD to your local filesystem - Works fully offline with no internet Before building this I tried every local AI app I could find, but it seemed each one had different problems. The main thing I noticed is that none of them could do what the ChatGPT and Claude apps do with your files, e.g. read and change files in a folder, look at images, run code in a sandbox, draw a chart. The most advanced thing any of them did was paste a plain text file into a small context window, which basically failed as soon as you had a file larger than a few KB. I couldn't find anything that could easily parse images and bigger PDFs. The OSS solutions that were more advanced all seemed to default to hosted models (either OSS or closed), which defeats the entire point of the privacy that on-device OSS offers. They also seemed to push towards an account/open-core style business. I build it using Electron bridged with llama.cpp in its own process. On initial load, the system will try and figure out if you have a compatible graphics card and if not default to CPU-only (I ran into a lot of issues of graphics card beeing seemingly compatible but then crashing on first query, there's a whole saga to this lol). Code execution happens in a sandbox that can only write to the chat's folder and has no network unless asked (sandbox-exec on macOS, Landlock on Linux and a low-integrity process on Windows). Images go to a small Qwen3-VL model. Dictation is a local Whisper model. The hardest part was definitely to get the smaller models to use tools reliably. Ran into a ton of issues of 4B models happily saying "here's your chart" without ever calling the chart tool or get stuck in an infinite call loop. I spent a fair amount of the work building guards vs tweaking prompts (that didn't really work for small models). I understand the pushback that local models are weaker than frontier cloud models. This is true, but for most tasks for most normal people, I'd argue you rarely need the newest frontier model. From my own evals, systems with 16+ GB of RAM do really well, and if you have a GPU or more RAM, you get very close to what you'll get out of the box with a frontier hosted model. Excited to hear what you think and see how it runs on other systems!

projects.title: Show HN: Markdown is 40× more token-efficient with SQLite
projects.author: richardcrng
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Richard, founder of Native. I'm working on open-source context ownership, to stop AI centralisation: https://github.com/withnative/native My first focus has been making Markdown vaults powerful enough so that teams can self-host all of their context (messaging, docs and projects), without it being externally fragmented or rate-limited. I'm sharing some early results: Markdown vaults can be 40× more efficient with SQLite! https://www.withnative.ai/research-and-posts/markdown-contex... Here's some of the main ideas: - SQLite or Markdown folders, you pick. You can project the same authoritative event log into either form; more projection formats will follow (e.g. maybe neo4j; we do use a graph structure). - Empirically: SQLite is better for agents! On a 120 trial evaluation for 11,000 records, agents use 40× fewer tokens with SQLite vs Markdown, per correct answer. - Everything is a file or SQLite row. Messages, documents and projects: all can be modelled in your vault. You get local-first collaboration with teammates, synced to a cloud of your choice. - You can render your vault with arbitrary UI. Your WhatsApp-like UI speaks to your teammate's Slack-like UI; both are just views over the same database. A few things I've learned building this: - Agents do pretty well even without SQL if you give them strongly typed Markdown frontmatter. This was one arm of the trial I ran. I didn't have any clear expectations, but it was cool to watch: agents ended up writing Python scripts to do SQL-like queries. - Cumulatively, cached input tokens can get expensive. I feel silly in hindsight here. I'd gotten used to letting my sessions run long, "It's all cached so it's very cheap". But when I looked at my results here, over 2/3 of the token bill on long sessions was cached input... - "Markdown vaults don't scale as well as databases" isn't as self-evident as I think. This is why I decided to benchmark it... I've had some very blank stares when I try to explain how Markdown files might break at true agent-scale volume. Unfortunately, the dataset is private, because it's two months of my own work. I am considering open-sourcing it even so, but there is definitely some embarrassing stuff in there. TBD... I know that independent result verification matters! The core engine that I evaluated is open-source, with more to be released soon: https://github.com/withnative/native If you're interested in trying connected context on an open engine, you can get updates from our website or email me directly: richard@withnative.ai https://www.withnative.ai/

projects.summary: ## 提前缓存，没网照样玩 飞飞掼蛋，是我做给朋友的一张随身牌桌。飞机上、地下室、深山里，没带扑克牌时，也想用手机来一局。 ### 没有外网，怎么玩？ 出发前，每台手机先联网打开游戏，确认‘离线资源已保存’。 - 一个人：缓存后可直接和3位电脑练习。 - 朋友一起：各自缓存好，再连接同一个可互通的 Wi-Fi 或手机热点，选择‘附近离线’，完成邀请与回应的双向扫码。多人仍需要设备间连接，当前网页版不支持纯蓝牙联机。 - 有互联网：各用自己的5G或Wi-Fi，选择‘在线快捷’，扫一次座位邀请就能加入，不要求同一个网络。 机上无线使用请遵守航司规定；酒店公共Wi-Fi可能隔离设备。多人局请房主保持页面前台。 ### 一到四人，都能开桌 缺位由电脑补齐，可指定对家。上传头像、改昵称，让牌友一眼认出你；20款个人背景各自选择，横竖屏自动适配。 进贡、还贡由玩家自行选择，支持内贡、双大王抗贡；本局打几，红桃对应级牌不能进贡。连续点‘提示’可轮换合法牌型；轮到谁会显示座位关系和名字，并提供语音提醒。两首独立背景音乐、快捷对话和表情，为牌桌添点热闹。 ### 人多时，也能办团建赛 支持8—32人的固定双人队，积分赛、淘汰赛、决赛与季军赛。团建联机目前是试用：队长手动录分、双方确认后计分，尚不自动收取各桌成绩。 ### 试玩与反馈 当前网页版免费试玩，无需注册。战绩保存在本机，可导出备份。iOS/安卓商店安装版与付费发行版尚未发布，不把计划中的功能当成已交付。实体手机兼容性和音画体验仍在持续验证。 制作人：飞飞。欢迎来玩，也欢迎提出具体修改建议。 反馈：shenpengfeisandy@gmail.com 公开反馈区：https://github.com/shenpengfeisandy-beep/feifei-guandan-feedback/issues 二维码打开的是游戏首页；加入朋友牌桌，请由房主在游戏里另发座位邀请。

projects.title: 独立站除了公开邮箱和微信二维码，还能怎么跟访客说上话？
projects.author: martin2013
projects.summary: 背景：个人博客，Hugo 生成，扔在 Cloudflare Pages 上，没有后端也没有数据库。 一直没放联系方式，原因有两个。公开邮箱三天就被爬虫抓走，垃圾邮件到现在还没清完；放个人微信二维码，等于要求每个想留言的人先加好友——多数人不会加，包括我自己。 但「有人找我时能第一时间知道」这件事一直没解决。把能想到的方案挨个试了一遍，记一下结论，也顺便求个更优解。 ### 先把需求拆成三条 1. **访客侧**：不注册、不加好友，邮箱和手机最好都能不填。 2. **站主侧**：消息落到手机上，且不要求我为此多装一个 App 、多开一个后台。 3. **隐私侧**：访客说的是私事，服务端最好别存。 后面的评价都对着这三条，而不是对着功能表。 ### 一、评论系统 最省事的是 [Disqus]( https://disqus.com)，但国内加载不稳，页面上还会塞它自己的推荐位。[Waline]( https://waline.js.org)、[Twikoo]( https://twikoo.js.org)、[Artalk]( https://artalk.js.org) 这几个开源的体验好得多，代价是要自己部署服务端并配数据库——对纯静态博客来说，为了留言区维护一套后端不太划算。[Giscus]( https://giscus.app) 不用额外部署，基于 GitHub Discussions ，但访客得有 GitHub 账号，我这点读者里一半没有。 这类方案的定位很清楚：**适合文章下面的公开讨论，不适合私下的联系**。公示在评论区里的内容，没人会写自己的联系方式。 ### 二、客服 SaaS [Tawk.to]( https://www.tawk.to) 免费档很能打，[Crisp]( https://crisp.chat) 界面更精致，[Intercom]( https://www.intercom.com) 是企业定价。它们的设计前提是「客服坐席」：开面板、装 App 、配工作时间，脚本还会给页面加一两百 KB 。个人博客一天来不了几个访客，为它装个 App 不划算。 还有一个容易忽略的细节：访客常常在窗口资源加载完之前就走了。 ### 三、表单转邮件 [Formspree]( https://formspree.io) 这类把表单提交转成邮件，或者自己写个 Cloudflare Worker 转发。门槛低、够用，但「邮件」这个通道的时效性是硬伤：我一天开两次邮箱，访客发完就去干别的了。 适合非实时的需求收集（合作、反馈、投稿）。 ### 四、IM 中继 这一类是把消息推到站主本来就在用的聊天软件里。国内有几个成熟服务：[Server 酱]( https://sct.ftqq.com)、[PushPlus]( https://www.pushplus.plus)、[WxPusher]( https://wxpusher.zjiecode.com)，都是「一条 HTTP 请求 → 微信」的管道，最初是为服务器告警、脚本通知设计的。 注意它们解决的是「我主动推给自己」，不解决「访客说话」——这两件事经常被混为一谈。 要同时满足「访客能说话」和「站主在 IM 里回」，就得有个站内聊天页做入口。这类东西我找到的不是要自建就是半自建，最后我用的是[**信鸽**]( https://sendtk.com/?from=v2ex)：访客打开链接、填个称呼就能发消息（邮箱手机可选），消息进微信或 Telegram ，我引用那条消息回复就回到对应访客；聊天记录不落服务端，只存在访客浏览器里；嵌入是一行 iframe ，不用部署、不用配数据库。 ### 怎么选（按场景，不按谁更强） - 想让文章下面有人公开讨论：[Waline]( https://waline.js.org) / [Twikoo]( https://twikoo.js.org) / [Giscus]( https://giscus.app)。 - 有客服团队、要 SLA：[Tawk.to]( https://www.tawk.to) / [Crisp]( https://crisp.chat) / [Intercom]( https://www.intercom.com)。 - 只收非实时的合作邮件：[Formspree]( https://formspree.io) 这类表单转邮件。 - 只想「有人找我时，手机上立刻能回」：IM 中继这一类，前提是它有站内聊天页。 ### 说清楚立场 第四类那个工具（[**信鸽**]( https://sendtk.com/?from=v2ex)）是我做的，所以看到这一段时你可以打折听。它的短板我直接列： - 免费档每天 20 条消息（通知与聊天合计），流量一起来就不够； - 不是工单系统：没有历史归档、没有多人协作，服务端不存聊天记录，回头找对话只能翻微信； - 海外访客更适合走 Telegram ，纯微信适合站主人在国内。 前三类的链接与评价没有因为我要推自己的东西而改动。 ### 求教 你们站上现在放的是什么？有没有「访客零门槛 + 站主手机直达」的其它方案，我大概率漏了。

projects.title: [开源推荐] AWS Lightsail 流量池省钱计算器：算出加几台实例最划算
projects.author: yt1988

github.name: yt1988/lightsail-cost-saver
github.description: Free single-page calculator for AWS Lightsail data transfer pools: forecast overage and find the cheapest way to add bandwidth. 10 languages.

projects.summary: Lightsail 同地区、同规格的实例共享一个流量池，超额费每 TB 约 $92，而加一台 $5 的 IPv6 实例每 TB 只要 $2.5。这个纯前端工具帮你算清这笔账：填入本月已用流量，它会预测月底用量、额度哪天用完、会多付多少钱，并对比加 0～3 台实例的总花费，给出最省的方案。数据只存在浏览器本地。 亮点 规则来自官方文档和 AWS Support 的回答：入站出站都扣额度、只对出站超额收费、月中开通按小时折算、已产生的超额无法被新实例抵消；19 个地区的价格由脚本从 AWS Price List API 拉取，额度减半的地区也已算进去。 不只告诉你会不会超，还给出可执行的方案：额度预计哪天用完、加几台最省、比不加省多少，一键加进配置；只知道月总量时有整月规划模式。 能直接交给 AI Agent：站点提供 llms.txt，计算模块 calc.js 和 prices.json 都允许跨域读取，在 ChatGPT、Claude 等 Agent 或自己的脚本里调用，结果和网页完全一致。 纯静态单页、无后端，可以免费部署到 Cloudflare Workers 或 Vercel，也可以一行 docker run；计算核心有回归测试，在 CI 中运行。

projects.author: TaskWitness

github.name: GANGMU-SBOM/gangmu
github.description: Generate a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM for embedded C/C++ firmware from the build's compile database and linker map.

projects.summary: 我是 Gangmu（纲目）的发起人。它是一个面向嵌入式 C/C++ 的开源组件识别和 SBOM 工具。 芯片 SDK 中的第三方库经常被复制、改名或做厂商修改，源码目录中存在的代码也未必进入最终固件。Gangmu 使用社区维护的规则识别组件，可结合 compilecommands.json 和链接器 map 补充构建证据，区分源码存在、编译和链接信息，输出 CycloneDX/SPDX。 仓库提供对 GmSSL 改名、删除版本信息及修改源码的受控示例，供读者查看和复现。希望收集更多公开 SDK 的识别反馈与规则贡献。 工具采用 Apache-2.0，独立规则库采用 CDLA-Permissive-2.0。适合嵌入式开发、固件交付和软件供应链安全相关读者。 联系：64031875@qq.com

projects.title: 用 ONNX Runtime Web 把 AI 和弦识别放到了浏览器本地运行，做了个 Chord Finder
projects.author: limerain
projects.summary: 最近做了一个音乐相关的 Web 工具，ChordFold 。 地址： https://chordfold.com/ 主要功能是：用户选择一段 MP3 或 WAV 音频，AI 自动识别里面的和弦，以及和弦随时间的变化。 和一些需要上传音频到服务器的识别服务不同，我选择了浏览器本地推理的方案。 目前的技术方案： 使用 BTC 系列和弦识别模型 模型转换为 ONNX 格式 通过 ONNX Runtime Web 在浏览器里执行 WASM 推理 对音频进行解码和 CQT 特征提取 模型预测后对结果进行平滑，生成和弦时间轴 用户侧的操作流程也比较简单： 选择本地音频文件 首次使用时下载识别模型 在浏览器本地分析音频 得到按时间排列的和弦结果 点击时间轴上的和弦，可以跳到对应位置回听 可以切换查看支持的吉他和弦指法图、钢琴音符参考 目前限制音频最大 14MB 、最长 10 分钟。 选择本地推理主要有几个考虑： 第一，音频不需要上传服务器，相对更有隐私优势。 第二，不需要为每个用户的识别请求支付云端 GPU 推理费用。 第三，工具本身不需要用户注册账号。 但缺点也很明显。 首先，模型首次下载需要时间。 其次，不同设备上的 WASM 推理性能差异比较大。 还有就是和弦识别的准确率问题。对于干净的钢琴、吉他音频，相对容易分析；复杂编曲、失真、转位和弦以及快速切换的片段，模型仍然可能出现错误。 目前不打算宣传什么 99% 准确率，实际上还没有可靠的统一准确率测试数据。 接下来主要想继续优化识别效果、模型加载和结果交互。 想请教一下 V 友： 有没有做过音乐信息检索（ MIR ）或者音频模型部署的？ 对于浏览器本地音频推理，ONNX Runtime Web + WASM 还有哪些值得优化的方向？ 有更适合浏览器端运行、准确率又比较好的和弦识别模型推荐吗？ 如果你会弹吉他或者钢琴，也欢迎拿一段音频测试一下，看看识别效果怎么样。 技术交流和产品体验方面的建议都欢迎。

projects.title: 【工具自荐】【AESTHETICA-10】一个永远只打 10 分的 AI 颜值评分（恶搞）
projects.author: aeroxy
projects.summary: 2017 年我自己做过一个 AI 颜值打分应用。快十年过去了，又看见了类似的网站：上传一张自拍，给你算出一个精确到小数点后两位的分数，比如 6.2/10，再顺手卖你一套“变美方案”。自己亲手做过，我的结论是：这东西从根上就是扯淡。分数主要量的是你的相机，光线、焦距、角度、距离一变，同一张脸的分数就跟着变，有的网站干脆建议你多传几张取平均。还有研究发现，离脸 30 厘米拍的自拍，会让鼻翼看起来比 1.5 米外拍的宽约 30%（JAMA Facial Plastic Surgery，2018）。精确到两位小数只是看起来像科学，本质是带进度条的星座运势。 所以这次我做了一个反过来的版本：仪器感一样不少，只是结论比较诚实：你本来就是 10 分。 真·人脸识别：在浏览器里用 MediaPipe 人脸关键点模型定位 478 个面部关键点，把“黄金比例”网格、颧骨、下颌角的标注精准贴到你脸上，然后全部无视。识别不到人脸就不画网格，直接显示“NO FACE IN FRAME · STILL 10/10”。 核心评分算法只有一行：return 10.00; 5 位专家人设：严谨的颅面物理学博士、巴黎高定选角导演、15 世纪佛罗伦萨雕塑家、算力过载的神经网络集群、无条件夸夸的吹捧科学家。每位都有自己的一套夸法、六维评分和一张煞有介事的人体测量数据表。 官方认证 PDF：一键导出 A4 证书，带你的照片、病例编号、六维评分、专家签名和印章，可用于各种争论、群聊和照镜子。 多种测试对象：支持上传、拖拽、摄像头实时追踪（拍下一帧再打分），也可以直接用内置样本：凌晨 5 点枕头印自拍、死亡仰拍角度、车管所证件照，以及一颗土豆。 隐私方面，照片全程不出浏览器，人脸识别在本地运行，只从 CDN 下载模型文件。没有后端、不上传、不存储，没有登录也没有付费。界面目前是英文。

projects.title: Show HN: Reusable, spectraly shaped Blue Noise point clouds
projects.author: adec314
projects.summary: Blue noise is the task of sampling a collection of points optimally placed to cover space randomly yet uniformly. -randomly: no periodic pattern or undesired ordered structure, to prevent aliasing effects. -uniformly: no empty regions, clusters... that would unavoidably appear by just using a raw random generator because of natural fluctuations. In spectral language, one can take the Fourier transform of the point cloud. For a blue noise, it's amplitude should be: - 0 or small at low frequencies. This ensures long-range order. - 1 or not too big at high frequencies (short-range disorder). Hence blue noise: Imagine sending light on the point cloud; in some abstract sense, only the blue (high frequency) will pass through. Many popular algorithms can sample blue noise: Poisson disks, void and clusters, Lloyd relaxation... but the bluest blue noise (those that show up as a hard 0-1 spectral step) comes from the most basic, brute-force algorithm you can imagine. Take points from a purely random generator, compare the Fourier transform with the 0-1 target, launch gradient descent... and wait. Wait because it has O(N^2) complexity. Well, it turns out in 2D / 3D, advanced fast Fourier techniques can bring it down to N log N, see https://github.com/martiniani-lab/FReSCo (not me), but this is limited to 2D / 3D point clouds. So, all this just to say that I launched a high-quality but slow blue noise optimiser on the GPU, collected the samples in a reusable database and hope it could interest people from graphics, statistical physics, maybe also quasi-Monte Carlo integration (but this one is just a maybe, simple Sobol sequences are better than blue noise on many tasks) or just curious hackers. Sampled clouds, all open access: 2D to 32D 1k to 130k points (and up to 30 millions in 2D / 3D thanks to the mentioned fast Fourier speed-up).

projects.summary: 公司制度文档散在网盘、群聊、个人电脑，新人问、老人答，答的不一定是现行版本。试过 SaaS 知识库，卡在「数据出内网」和「按人头收费」两点，就自己写了一个。 只做一件事：把 Markdown 丢进 docs/，就能提问，回答带《文档》/章节出处，能点开核对原文；文档带可见范围（普通员工查不到财务制度，财务角色能看到）。全程不联网，零第三方依赖，一个文件 380 行。 几个实现上的小设计： - 分块：维护标题栈 + 段落，约 420 字一块，每块自带「《员工报销制度》/ 报销标准」这样的路径，回答时直接当引用 - 中文分词：二元组切分，不依赖分词库，英文数字按词切 - 召回：BM25 + TF-IDF 双路加权。第一版问「出差住宿报销上限」，第一条返回的是「差旅餐补」——加「查询词覆盖率」加权后才稳定命中住宿段落 - 回答默认抽取式，不生成。制度类问题最怕编造，返回原文让人自己核对 部署就两条命令：`python3 kb.py ingest` 建索引，`python3 kb.py serve` 起服务，目录拷到内网机器就能用。 演示（ 89 秒纯录屏）： https://youtu.be/cNloexteD4s 实现细节长文： https://juejin.cn/spost/7699848140908544010 代码： https://github.com/luobobo896 轻喷。主要想听检索排序和文档权限这两块还有哪些坑，或者你们公司现在怎么解决「制度找不到」这个问题。

projects.summary: 测试同学大概都熟悉这个场景：需求文档一到手，就得人肉把 PRD 一条条翻译成用例表；好不容易写完，接口/UI 自动化脚本又因为一次改版全部失效。我们被这件事折磨了太多年，干脆把整条链路 AI 化做成了平台，今天自荐给大家——WHartTest。 它是一个可自部署的 AI 测试自动化平台（协议为自定义，见仓库 LICENSE），基于 Django + Vue 前后端分离，GitHub 目前 1.1k star。 它主要做三件事： 功能用例：上传需求文档（支持在线编辑），AI 结合知识库上下文生成完整用例（前置/步骤/预期），列表 + 思维导图双视图管理 接口自动化：根据接口定义自动生成请求步骤、断言、变量提取与前后置脚本；失败后 AI 读日志和响应定位问题，给出修复方案 UI 自动化：AI 生成页面操作步骤与元素定位，执行时采集日志/截图/视频/Trace，定位失效自动给修复建议 底座是 LangChain/LangGraph 多轮编排 + RAG 知识库（文档分块/向量化/重排）+ MCP 工具调用，另有一个 Skills 技能库，可以装 Playwright 技能让 AI 真正操作浏览器。

projects.author: Doublzzz

github.name: Doublzzz/FactoryFlow
github.description: Small-factory orders, deliveries and reconciliation. Local-first Windows developer preview.

projects.summary: 我平时做制造贸易相关业务，要接订单、安排送货、月底对账。借助 AI 编程工具，我把这些流程做成了 FactoryFlow（交有数），现以 MIT 许可证开源，提供 Windows 开发者预览版。 GitHub 源码、说明和演示 · Windows 预览版下载 目前围绕三个环节： 录单：可以从第一张订单开始，客户和物料资料逐步整理；图片、PDF 的本地 OCR 结果需要人工核对后确认。 分批送货：按订单行记录已交、待交和各自单位。送货录错可以作废，恢复待交数量并保留原记录。 对账：记录客户反馈、部分认可、本期正式结算和跨月承接，保留历史凭证。 数据保存在本机，核心业务与本地 OCR 可以离线运行。使用 React / TypeScript、Python / FastAPI 和 PostgreSQL；数量与金额采用精确小数，业务动作保留审计记录。 合成数据示例：120 件已交 30 件、剩 90 件；35.5 千克已交 10.25 千克、剩 25.25 千克。 当前公开包为 v0.1.0-preview.1，仅支持 Windows 10/11 x64、单机及人民币业务，尚不包含库存、付款、多币种和海外税务。代码、测试及文档有 AI 编程工具深度参与，我负责需求、业务规则和流程核对。 公开包完成过合成数据流程及备份恢复检查，仍不等于长期生产验证；OCR 可能漏行或识别错误。请在独立试用目录使用合成样例，不要放入唯一一份真实业务数据，预览版之间暂不保证直接沿用旧数据。 欢迎做过跟单、送货、对账或业务系统的朋友试用，指出缺少的业务情况和不顺手的操作。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Acard：可以本地运行的开源 Notion，自带 MCP，让 AI 直接读写你的笔记

github.name: Hakubisual/open-notion-acard
github.description: Acard - the open Notion you can run locally. Self-hosted server + desktop app, AGPL-3.0.

projects.summary: 先说明一下：我是 Acard 的维护者，也在负责它的内测，所以这是一条自荐。 Acard 是一个开源（AGPL-3.0）、本地优先的 Notion 式工作区。一个 Bun 进程跑起编辑器和接口，所有数据都存在你自己选定文件夹里的 SQLite 文件中，不开云功能就不会有任何东西离开你的电脑。 做它的初衷很简单：我平时大量的想法和资料其实都是在和 AI 的对话里产生的，但这些内容最后总是散落在聊天记录里。与其再手动整理进 Notion 或 Obsidian，不如让 AI 直接把对话写成页面。 主要功能： 块编辑器：标题、列表、待办、折叠块、引用、代码、表格、公式、图片，支持 / 命令和 Markdown 快捷键，可以分 2–4 栏排版。 数据库：表格、看板、画廊、列表、日历、时间线、图表 7 种视图，支持关联、汇总和公式。 内置 MCP 和 REST API：在本机运行时，Claude Code、Codex 等 MCP 客户端无需 token 就能直接读写页面，例如 claude mcp add --transport http acard 导入导出：支持 Markdown 和 Notion 导出文件。 备份：一个 zip 包含所有表、文件和每个页面的 Markdown 副本，每天自动备份。 团队使用：在局域网、家里的服务器或 VPN 上跑一个服务端，其他人用浏览器或桌面端连接。 界面支持简体中文、英文、韩文。 安装：Windows 可以直接下载 Acard Local 安装包（目前还没签名，SmartScreen 会提示，点「更多信息 → 仍要运行」即可）；macOS / Linux 需要从源码构建，或者直接 bun local/main.ts 跑服务端用浏览器打开。

projects.title: 【工具自荐】【量化学院】面向零基础的交互式量化交易入门课
projects.author: aeroxy
projects.summary: 总有人问我量化交易到底是什么，大家总把它想象成某种高深莫测的黑魔法、天才数学模型或者电脑自动印钞机。其实底层逻辑真没那么玄乎：把一个直觉写成计算机能执行的死规则，老老实实用历史数据做回测验证，再做好仓位控制别把自己玩死，仅此而已。为了不每次都从头解释一遍，我干脆做了这个互动式小课。 为了让任何人都能完全看懂，课程把核心概念全做成了可互动的沙盒实验： 猜涨跌小游戏：连猜 10 天明天的走势，亲身体会单日涨跌基本就是抛硬币，量化赚的是几千次交易里 53% 胜率的微小优势。 动量与均值回归回测：拖动滑块调均线和布林带参数，切换趋势市和震荡市，实时看“$100 变成多少”的净值曲线和买卖点，看懂震荡市里双均线是怎么来回打脸被割韭菜的。 夏普比率与回撤对比：直观展示为什么一个赚 +120% 但中途腰斩 50% 的策略，在专业量化眼里远不如一个年化 +30% 但回撤只有 5% 的平稳策略。 40 人凯利公式下注模拟：给每人一枚 55% 胜率的硬币，只要每次下注超过 20%（重仓），典型玩家最后全都会走向事实破产。 过拟合陷阱实时演示：在一段 100% 纯随机的数据里自动扫 430 组参数，选出在“过去”暴赚的所谓“神级策略”，然后一揭晓“未来”数据，当场打回原形。 10 行 Python 代码拆解：点击每行看逐行注释，重点解释为什么 .shift(1) 是防止“偷看未来数据”（未来函数 Bug）的铁律。 市场走势基于 PRNG 伪随机数算法生成，无需任何后端或外部网络请求，完完全全在浏览器本地单页跑通。 页面支持全量 EN / 中文 一键即时切换（包括图表标签、报错解释与交互反馈），词汇表支持中英双向搜索，进度自动存 localStorage。没有登录、没有付费、没有真实资金风险。

projects.title: Show HN: Sparse kernel delivering 36% higher training throughput

projects.summary: I developed a custom GPU kernel in Triton to accelerate training with a sparse feed-forward network (FFN). The kernel has so far been tested on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU and requires GPU hardware with BF16 support. Whether a model trained with a sparse FFN and densified afterwards can match the quality of a model trained densely remains an open question. These early results have motivated me to continue training a larger model using this approach. More about EUGEN and my work: https://jakubcwirlej.com/ai-dev/

projects.title: [开源推荐] AKDesk Fixed：本地优先的固收研究工作台（作者自荐）
projects.author: raistlinsha-plus

github.name: raistlinsha-plus/akdesk-fixed
github.description: Open-source fixed-income briefs with provenance. Try the static demo, then run the local-first AKShare & macro research workstation on macOS.

projects.summary: AKDesk Fixed 是一个本地优先的固收与宏观研究工作台，面向个人研究者和关注金融数据的开发者。它将资金利率、收益率曲线和国债期货的公开数据整理成带来源、时点和状态的一页简报，支持临时备注、Markdown 导出与打印/PDF。本地版还包含自选、信用观察、研究项目和专题复盘，主要适配 Apple Silicon Mac，界面以中文为主。 亮点 围绕具体任务组织功能：查看市场变化 → 回到收益率曲线核验 → 添加备注并导出一页简报。中国市场基础路径不需要 FRED 或 AI Key。 展示数据来源、观测和抓取时间，区分缓存、过期、演示及混合来源；缺失值保持为空，不用零代替，也不自动生成投资结论。 提供无需安装的在线体验和可复现 CLI 案例，帮助不熟悉固收业务的开发者理解金融数据如何转化为研究底稿。 自有代码采用 MIT 协议，技术栈为 React/TypeScript/Vite、FastAPI/Python 和 SQLite；研究资料保存在本机，没有使用遥测或追踪 SDK。 当前版本为 v1.1.0。在线演示使用固定的 2026-08-03 合成样例，不连接真实行情服务；本地完整版通过 AKShare 等数据源获取公开数据，不承诺交易所授权实时行情或机构级 SLA。MIT 许可不包含第三方行情数据的再分发权，产品不构成投资建议。

projects.title: Show HN: Dánwò – Open-source E2E testing with emulators and fault injection
projects.author: faithfulojebiyi
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Faithful. I built dánwò, an open-source (Apache-2.0) end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps, written in TypeScript. The problem: a UI test can click "Pay", see "Payment successful" and pass, while the card was charged twice, the webhook was handled twice, or the receipt email never went out. With coding agents writing more of our code, that gap between "the screen looks right" and "the right things happened" is where I kept finding bugs. How it works: - Tests drive the app like a user, with locators or plain-English agent steps. An agent step calls a model once; danwo records the actions and replays them on later runs with no model calls, so CI doesn't need an API key. - Your app runs behind an egress proxy. Calls to Stripe, Clerk, Resend, Slack, Google and about 20 other providers are answered by local emulators at the real hostnames, so there are no sandbox keys and no code changes. For Node apps a preload routes the calls; Bun honours HTTPS_PROXY. - An invariant is a check that runs after the test and compares two sides: what the provider says happened (charges, emails, messages) and what your app stored. For example, credits granted must equal paid checkouts times 500. - `danwo matrix` replays a test once per fault it could meet: a 500 or 429 from a provider, a declined card, a duplicate, late, forged or replayed webhook, a double-submit, a database commit whose reply is lost, Postgres unreachable for a few seconds. The invariant judges every run, so you see exactly which failure your app mishandles. - Every run leaves a flight record: video, each step, every provider call, webhook delivery and database statement, with secrets redacted. It runs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and on the Android emulator and iOS Simulator. It ships an MCP server and a skill, so coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) can write and run tests and fix what fails. Limitations, honestly: the emulators are only as good as their fidelity to the real APIs. Each one has a suite that runs against the real provider to catch drift, but they won't cover every edge of Stripe's API. Backend routing is built for Node and Bun today. Mobile tests need macOS or Linux. It's early (v0.1.2). The name is Yorùbá: "dán an wò" means "try it and see". Quickstart: npx @danwo/cli init (docs: https://danwo.dev/docs/quickstart ) I'd love feedback, especially on faults you've been bitten by that aren't in the matrix yet.

projects.title: [开源推荐] WPAForge - 在手机上审计自家 Wi-Fi 的弱口令
projects.author: wlmosv-png

github.name: wlmosv-png/wpaforge
github.description: Android 原生 WPA/WPA2 密码审计工具：按 SSID 现场派生候选而非翻大字典，逐条真实关联验证，只认同一行里的 4-Way Handshake 完成。含 WPS 四层候选与拆半攻击、局域网侦察、.cap/.hc22000 离线校验。纯 Root。 | Native Android WPA/WPA2 audit tool: SSID-derived candidate generation, handshake-only verification, WPS, LAN recon. Root only.

projects.summary: WPAForge 是一个跑在安卓手机上的 WPA/WPA2 弱口令审计工具，开源（Apache-2.0），需要 Root。 它不翻几百万条的通用字典，而是按目标路由器的 SSID 现场派生候选——比如路由器叫 FASTE972，它就先生成 FASTE972、faste972、97297297、e9721188 这些，几百条覆盖常见命名习惯，再按目标特征排序，最可能的排最前。命中通常发生在第几十条，而不是第几万条。 每条候选都真的向目标 AP 发一次关联请求，不模拟、不猜测；判定只认一种证据：4-Way Handshake 完成，且 SSID、supplicant 状态、IP 三条同源于同一条记录，所以不会有“假成功”。 其他：进度实时存盘、中断能接着跑、锁屏继续；多目标后台队列；内置 IEEE OUI 表（15913 条），列表里直接显示水星 / 中兴 / 腾达 / 迅捷等厂商名。 要求：Android 8.0+、Root。适用范围仅限你自己拥有或已获明确授权的网络——对自家路由器是排查弱口令，对别人的网就是违法，这条边界很清楚。 亮点 1. 不用电脑、不用外置网卡、不用 Termux —— 安卓原生，一台 Root 手机跑完全流程。传统路子要笔记本 + 支持监听模式的网卡 + Kali，这套只要一个 APK。 2. 按目标 SSID / BSSID 现场派生候选，而不是翻大字典。派生维度：SSID 原文与大小写变形、里面数字串的重复与加后缀、去掉分隔符的合并串、SSID 与高频数字的多种拼接、BSSID 尾号族，再叠通用弱口令与厂商规则。几百条排在队列最前面，通常第几十条就命中。 3. 判定链只认一种证据：SSID 逐字相等 + supplicant COMPLETED + 有效 IP。而且刻意不让 netId 参与判定 —— 早期把它当否决条件时出过真实事故：密码是对的、系统确实连上了，却因为 netId 时序对不上而整段跳过成功判断。netId 现在只作为证据强度标注。宁可报「不确定」，也不报假成功。 4. 断点续跑 + 后台队列 + 锁屏继续。进度实时存盘，多目标排队自动跑，每项可单独暂停。 5. 内置 IEEE OUI 表 15913 条，扫描列表直接显示「水星 / 中兴 / 腾达 / 迅捷 / 四川天邑康和」，随机化 MAC 单独标注，不和「未收录」混着显示。 6. 核心判定与派生全是纯逻辑，不依赖 Android —— 可以离线跑单测。 7. Apache-2.0，无广告、无内购、不上传任何数据。

projects.title: 做了一个 PHP2Shell 应急辅助工具：被动响应头检查、版本核对和配置引导
projects.author: Tim99
projects.summary: 最近做了一个 PHP2Shell 应急辅助网站，把公开响应头检查、PHP 版本比较和临时缓解配置整理到了一起，想分享给有 PHP 网站需要维护的朋友。 地址： https://checkphp2shell.com/ 目前主要有几个功能： - 输入公开域名，查看响应头是否暴露 PHP 版本，以及是否存在 PHP 、Laravel 、WordPress 等相关线索。 - 识别 Cloudflare 、Sucuri 、Akamai 、CloudFront 等边缘服务的公开标记。 - 手动输入实际 PHP 版本，核对修复版本门槛，并查看不同部署环境的配置示例。 - 提供 php.ini 、Nginx 、Apache 、Cloudflare WAF 、ModSecurity 、Docker/K8s 的配置引导。 想先把检测边界讲清楚：**它检查的是公开响应头，结果只能作为排查线索。** 对目标网站只发送普通 HEAD 请求，遇到明确不支持 HEAD 的响应时才回退 GET ，不发送漏洞利用载荷或 multipart POST ，也不跟随重定向。 响应头可能被隐藏、修改或缓存，因此： - 没有发现 PHP 特征，不能证明网站没有使用 PHP 。 - 显示的版本达到修复门槛，不能确认实际软件包和所有 Web worker 都已更新。 - 发现 Cloudflare 等标记，不能确认 WAF 已启用，更不能确认规则能够覆盖相关攻击。 - 外部检查无法读取内部 php.ini ，也无法确认网站此前是否遭到入侵。 另外，页面里刻意区分了**临时缓解和完整修复**。 INI 配置和 WAF 规则可以在适用条件下降低部分攻击路径的风险，但不能当成完整修复。完整修复仍需要应用官方修复版本或经厂商确认的安全补丁，并验证实际处理 Web 请求的 PHP 实例和 worker 都已经使用修复后的构建。CLI 的 `php -v` 也可能与网站实际运行的 PHP 不同。 配置生成前需要重新确认版本、部署方式和适用前提，响应头里的版本不会自动被当成已经核实的服务器环境。 网站目前支持英语、日语、德语、西班牙语和葡萄牙语。欢迎大家试用，尤其想听听：结果说明是否容易理解、配置引导有没有遗漏，以及哪些措辞可能让人误以为“检查通过就代表安全”。

projects.title: Show HN: Cryptex Vault – A password manager designed to outlive its creator
projects.author: Bl4cksmith
projects.summary: Hello everyone! About four years ago, a password manager I've used and depended on has been acquired and soon after, it was shut down. If anyone remembers MYKI, it was a password manager that stood out at the time. It didn't require an email address and a password for registration and it synchronized credentials peer-to-peer. It was quite handy so a couple of my friends and I got hooked, and were using it up until the last day it was online. The thing was, I didn't want to change password managers to other options available at the time, none felt right - I wanted to stay.. So I did what any sensible engineer would do 4 years ago and I wrote my own. I moved all my credentials there as soon as I had a first version ready. It was ugly (God knows I had UI/UX skills to learn), but it worked. Soon after, the same friends that were using MYKI switched over to using Cryptex Vault. I get why, we had the same P2P synchronization across devices, it was simple and didn't try to be the most-feature complete application out there - it did the job. That was an exciting moment. So exciting, in fact, that I've posted to HN to tell people about it. At the time, I had a weird thing for decentralization so I called it a "Fully Decentralized Password Manager". Three years go by, I keep maintaining the project, with no real intention of proper marketing or polishing. At one point I checked the usage and figured out that a handful of people (and their families) were still using Cryptex Vault as their password manager. Three months ago, I left my comfy job as lead software engineer at a local company to dedicate time to a company I called Cryptex Industries. Polished Cryptex Vault, cleaned it up, made it open source, started providing Docker images for self-hosting and included some of the features I've only used internally (ssh-agents). That way Cryptex Industries need not remain operational for users to have a path to continued use! To make the project commercially viable, I started offering managed services through the Online Services plan. By using Online Services you remove the operational burden of self-hosting and infrastructure maintenance from yourself while still getting the same benefits: Managed backup storage, synchronization between devices, sharing, ssh-agents, device management. It is convenience, not access to core features. The core application is free and you can use it with no subscriptions of any kind, whatsoever. It's P2P synchronized, with industry-standard crypto choices including post-quantum primitives for synchronization - https://www.cryptex-vault.com/docs/cryptography It has importers for popular password managers, along with autofill for chromium browsers (firefox is a todo, yell and I'll get on it). As for the platforms, there is a web app, an android application and an ssh-agent for linux (will put it up on AUR when they open up registrations again). Feel free to try it out (there is a 14-day trial for managed services!), self-host it or break it. I would appreciate your thoughts on this and I wish you a nice friday!

projects.title: Show HN: whytime: time(1) that tells you where the wall-clock time went
projects.author: Arinerron
projects.summary: time says a command took 3.8 seconds... whytime tells you where those seconds went: $ sudo whytime -- sh -c 'sleep 0.5; dd … oflag=dsync; curl -s -o /dev/null https://speed.cloudflare.com/…' wall 3.83s 47% blocked on network: speed.cloudflare.com:443 (1 connection) 34% fsync on ~/.cache 13% timer sleep (sleep) 4% on-CPU (curl) 2% other The lines always add up to 100%. When the command waits on a child or another thread, whytime follows whoever woke it up, so a shell waiting on curl is charged to the network wait curl was stuck on. The top line is what you'd have to make faster. It can also draw a flamegraph. Uses eBPF (Linux 5.18+)

projects.title: Show HN: Ternlux – Free, local-first, bring-your-own-key AI pipeline builder
projects.author: sdataengineer
projects.summary: For the past 12 years as a data engineer, I've been building pipelines across many different business categories and sizes. Most pipelines that I’ve encountered were relatively simple jobs and required more orchestration and infrastructure than the work seems to justify. I wanted to make it easier for business users or analysts to take on the less complicated requests and technical engineers be able to focus on more complex pipelines. So in the past year I've been building a local desktop application (Mac/PC/Linux) to make it easy enough for analysts to build pipelines and answer analytical questions they have about their data, no matter their level of technical expertise. It’s called Ternlux, and it streamlines the process of transforming and getting your data where it needs to go. There are two key features: - Ask questions: AI helps to write the query for your connection and answer your question - Build reusable workflows: The AI generates SQL, Python, and workflow logic that executes based on your defined rules and triggers One of the key advantages of the application is you can perform cross-database joins between databases, local files, vector databases, and cloud storage. You describe the workflow you want and the app writes the code and builds the environment to execute it in (for local joins, it uses either JS, Python, or DuckDB to execute the code). For example, if I want to build a workflow that joins a Postgres table with a CSV file and write the results to Snowflake, I just describe the tables I want to use, the keys to join on, and where the join should run. The app takes care of the rest. I also wanted the app to be as secure as possible. It always asks for approval before performing any database or local file manipulation. It never sends anything to Ternlux servers if you haven’t opted into telemetry. It’s important to note that the app will send query results to your selected AI provider to analyze and answer your questions. It will also send the schema and a small sample size of your data to build workflows properly. It is a bring your own key application. It supports Gemini, Claude, OpenAI, and any models that are OpenAI compatible (Ollama, LM Studio, Openrouter…). All of your credentials stay encrypted locally. And the app is completely free including all features (besides the AI models you use with your own key obviously). I’ve built a quick demo showcasing the applications Demo: https://www.ternlux.com/online-demo/ 3-min overview: https://youtu.be/tA7N7wiLliA The list of connectors that exist: Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake, MongoDB, Pinecone, LanceDB, S3, GCS, Azure Blob, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, and Google Sheets. I would love your honest feedback on this. How can this product be improved? Would you currently use it as a tool to replace your current tool or in conjunction with your other tools? What feature do you find most useful and I should focus on from the list?

Web、CLI、TUI 三種操作方式：提供網頁介面、命令列工具及全螢幕終端介面，適合不同使用習慣與伺服器管理情境。 2. 不只是檔案分享：支援檔案、資料夾、程式碼片段、Markdown 筆記與連結，內建語法高亮、圖表渲染及內容預覽。 3. 多 S3 儲存池與容量溢出切換：可整合多個 S3 相容儲存空間，當單一儲存空間達到設定容量上限時，自動將後續上傳導向其他可用空間，充分利用不同儲存服務的容量額度。 4. 分享內容自動清理：可設定有效期限、下載次數與存取密碼，降低過期分享的管理成本。 5. 完整的自架管理功能：支援使用者權限、儲存配額、OIDC 登入、管理後台及多種資料庫。 6. 彈性的儲存與部署：支援本地磁碟、S3 相容儲存等後端，並可透過 Docker 部署；大檔案可直傳物件儲存，減少伺服器中轉壓力。

projects.title: 做了近 10 年合租车主，我开源了自己的订阅账本 Calends
projects.author: enann
projects.summary: 哈喽大家好，我是之前开发 [AppStorePrice]( https://appstoreprice.org/) 的朋友，这次给大家推荐一款订阅管理的开源方案：Calends 。 我自己一直都是订阅记录的重度用户，前前后后用过市面上十多款 App 、开源项目。但是用下来，总觉得它们跟我的实际需求，尤其是合租的场景不太匹配。YouTube 我开车快 10 年了，Spotify 也开了 5 年多。除了记录自己订了什么、花了多少钱，还要记成员付到哪天、哪些钱没收、自己到底垫了多少。再加上跨区、涨价、代付、礼品卡，很多细节都得另外补。 所以这次干脆自己做了一个，把这些年一直想要的功能都做进去。对于我自己的订阅和开车需求，我觉得目前没有比它更合适的了。尤其是现在的 AI 订阅。先放一段视频，大家可以直接看一下整体效果： [观看宣传视频]( https://media.calends.date/launch/2026-10-22/index.html) · [MP4 直链]( https://media.calends.date/launch/2026-10-22/calends-intro.16079708908f.mp4) ![Calends：AI 、合租、代付、多币种和余额续航]( https://media.calends.date/launch/2026-10-22/images/00-launch.8fe81ddc5174.png) ## 我最想说的，还是 AI 和 MCP 现在做软件，我觉得很重要的一点，就是有没有把 Agent 作为一等公民，能不能让 AI 真正帮我把事情做掉。所以在我的这个项目里，基础的 AI 创建、查询、维护订阅这些我都做了，接上自己的 DeepSeek API Key 或兼容服务就能用，收据也可以直接交给它整理，核对后添加。模型调用按你使用的平台计费。 然后是 MCP 。这可以让 Codex 、Claude Code 、Grok Bot 都可以接进来，直接管理自己的订阅账本。我现在的订阅就是交给 Grok Bot 帮我管理的。给了它邮箱权限，再接上 Calends 的 MCP ，每次有新的订阅邮件进来，就让它分析邮件，该新增的新增，该更新的更新，不用我再一条条照着填。 如果你是第一次用，直接让有邮箱权限的 AI 助手去分析历史邮件，把里面的订阅整理出来，查重、核对之后导入就行。如果你之前已经在用其他订阅管理 App ，也可以让能操作手机的 Codex 读取里面的订阅详情，再帮你导入自己的 Calends 。邮箱和手机由你接入的外部助手读取，账本这边通过 MCP 配合它完成录入。 ![Codex 、Claude Code 、Grok Bot 等 AI 助手可以通过 MCP 接入]( https://media.calends.date/launch/2026-10-22/images/02-mcp-clients.cd5cc6dca268.png) ## 还有一些功能，大家看看有没有这些痛点 **我订阅了 iCloud 土耳其区，但是它老涨价，涨价之前的价格怎么记？** 我自己这条 iCloud+，已经从 ₺64.99 涨到 ₺129.99 、₺249.99 ，再到 ₺399.99 。每次涨价的日期、之前多少钱，都能保留下来。切到原币看，也能把涨价和汇率变化分开。 ![我这条 iCloud+ 土耳其区订阅的三次调价记录]( https://media.calends.date/launch/2026-10-22/images/08-subscription-history.c40d149f78b7.png) **Spotify 开了这么多年，我到底总共付出去多少钱，收回来多少钱，亏了还是赚了？** 合租的支出、成员收款、谁付到哪天，都放在一起记。有人按月付，有人一次付半年，也能看清楚还有哪些钱没收到。 **我今天帮朋友续了 ChatGPT ，他上个月的钱付了没有？** 这种就单独记成代付，记到对应的人，收没收、收了多少都能查，也不会把替别人垫的钱算成自己的订阅消费。 **我打折买了礼品卡，面值是这么多，但实际花的钱又不一样，怎么算？** 面值和实际买入成本分开记。卡包里也可以管理支付方式、币种和余额，按后面的扣款估算还能用多久。还有一个很容易忽略的细节：我填的余额到底是哪天的余额？上周查到的数，不能一直当成今天的数，所以余额也专门做了校准日期。 包括汇率，我也专门接了。历史上每次付款，都可以按付款当天的汇率折成人民币，知道那一笔大概花了多少钱。 时间线、续费日历、各种报告图表也都做了。年付的订阅，可以分别看这个月付出去了多少钱、这个月分摊了多少费用；钱花在哪，也可以像看股票热力图那样看每个订阅占了多少。这些看起来都是小功能，但自己长期记订阅、开合租车的时候，确实都会用到，所以我把它们都补上了。 ## 部署和体验 可以直接用 Docker ，放到自己的服务器、NAS 上；也可以用 Cloudflare 账号部署到 Workers + D1 ，个人用量在免费额度内就能免费运行。支持备份恢复和 CSV 导入导出。 - 官网： https://calends.date - 文档： https://docs.calends.date - Demo： https://demo.calends.date - GitHub： https://github.com/imetn/calends 最后，我还专门做了一个彩蛋。**Claude 封号这个事情，我到底被封了几个号？有没有退款？没退的话，到底损失了多少钱？** 这些也可以记。我专门做了一个 [Claude 演示站]( https://demo.calends.date/claude/)，把账号停止、退款、没用完的时长和损失都放进去，大家可以直接进去看。演示站用的是虚构数据，主要给大家演示一下这种被封号的账怎么记。 其实我直接建议，这些事情全都交给 AI 就好了，让他帮我记录好我自己的订阅账，而且我测试下来，自己反代出来的 Deepseek 模型已经完全足够了，本身多模态也支持。粘贴上传图片记录订阅也是一个非常棒的体验。 一不小心说了这么多，总之吧，我觉得大家感兴趣可以去演示站试用一下看看，不关你是上百辆合租的车主，还是中转站几百个 Claude 账号的老板，都可以看看当前的方案能不能满足你的需求好好 项目是 MIT 开源的。如果有些场景还满足不了你的需求，欢迎直接提 [Issue]( https://github.com/imetn/calends/issues)，也欢迎 PR 。如果你自己想做深度定制，直接 fork ，搭自己的订阅账本就好。 如果你觉得这个项目有帮助，不妨在 GitHub 帮我点一个 Star ，这对我来说会非常有帮助。谢谢大家！

projects.title: 【工具自荐】remote-assist-tool：一个协助码，让 AI 助手直接调试远端机器
projects.author: kegechen

github.name: kegechen/remote-assist-tool
github.description: Remote assistance with a one-time code: let your AI agent (Claude Code, Codex…) debug a remote machine via MCP, or open an SSH tunnel. Relay / LAN / P2P, no public IP needed.

projects.summary: 我是 remote-assist-tool 的作者，提交给周刊编辑筛选。 remote-assist-tool 是一个命令行远程协助工具，Go 编写，单个二进制，MIT 协议开源。被协助的一方运行 remote share，拿到一个协助码；协助方用这个码就能连上去，不需要公网 IP，也不需要在对方机器上配置 SSH 服务端或开端口。 它有两种用法： 1. 传统 SSH 远程协助：协助方运行 remote help --code <协助码> --legacy-ssh，本地就有一条到对方 SSH 的隧道。 2. 让 AI 助手直接操作远端机器：remote help --mcp-stdio 本身就是一个标准的 MCP server，Claude Code、Codex、豆包等支持 MCP 的 AI 工具都能接入。配置好以后，对 AI 说一句"协助码 xxxx，连上去"，它就能在远端执行命令、读写文件、看进程、查日志、上传下载文件（一共 12 个工具），用来远程排查问题。被协助端的终端会实时显示 AI 执行的每一个操作。 bash 安装（Linux / macOS / Windows Git Bash，amd64 和 arm64 都支持） curl -fsSL | sh 被协助端：生成协助码，默认 30 分钟后过期 remote share 协助端：用协助码建立 SSH 隧道 remote help --code ABCD-EFGHIJ --legacy-ssh 其他特点： 三种连接方式：经公网中转服务器转发；同一局域网内用 --standalone 直连，不依赖任何外部服务器；NAT 打洞 P2P 直连，打洞失败会自动回落到中转。 中转服务器可以自己部署（Windows / Linux / macOS 都有预编译版本，Windows 还能装成系统服务）。也有一个内置的公共中转服务器，开箱即用，但它在海外，而且中转服务器属于信任边界，所以敏感环境建议自己部署。 链路使用 TLS 加密，AI 工具通道再用协助码派生的密钥额外加密一层；支持命令黑名单/白名单。

projects.author: edrin09

github.name: edrin09/boki
github.description: BOKI - offline-first open-source accounting software. Double-entry bookkeeping, multi-company isolation, plugin architecture, SQLite single-file. Data never leaves your machine. 离线优先的开源财务软件

projects.summary: BOKI 是一套离线优先的开源财务软件，前端 Vue 3 + 后端 NestJS + SQLite 单文件数据库，单命令启动、开箱即用。在云端记账簿数据泄露频发的当下，它走另一条路：没有云端、没有第三方 SDK、没有任何埋点与遥测——全部账务数据就是本机一个 financial.db 文件，备份是拷贝目录，迁移是搬文件夹，数据主权 100% 在用户手里。 内核只保留记账必需的复式记账引擎（科目、凭证、期初、公司上下文），借贷必相等由后端强校验；其余能力全部插件化（官方插件 14 个），不装的插件在界面上不留痕迹。 核心特性： 🧾 复式记账内核：科目 / 凭证 / 期初 / 多公司上下文，借贷必相等前后端双重强校验，已审核凭证禁止改动 📊 报表可审计：资产负债表、利润表（本期+本年累计）、科目余额表、试算平衡表、票据台账、现金流简表、费用结构分析 🔐 权限与多公司：JWT 登录 + RBAC（菜单级 + 操作级），一个账号管理多家记账公司，数据完全隔离 🗄 数据离线：SQLite 单文件（WAL 模式），一键备份/恢复，无任何外部服务依赖 🎤 语音识别离线：sherpa-onnx 本地流式中文 ASR（zipformer int8），音频不上传 🤖 大模型可选离线：内置 Ollama / llama.cpp / vLLM 本地模型预设（OpenAI 兼容协议、无需 API Key），也可切换云端模型 🧩 插件化：想要什么装什么，卸载不留痕迹 技术亮点： 复式记账引擎与权限模型在服务端强校验，不依赖前端约束 本地模型自动降级：模型缺失时服务照常启动，仅相关功能提示未就绪（/api/ocr/status 可查） 许可：内核 AGPL-3.0，官方插件 Apache-2.0 平台：Windows / macOS / Linux 适合对象：个人与小团队的记账、代理记账/财务工作室的私有化部署、对数据隐私敏感的任何记账场景。 项目正在寻找第一批真实用户，任何反馈（尤其是报表与记账流程上的"不顺手"）都非常欢迎，可以直接提 issue。如果觉得有价值，欢迎点个 Star 支持开源维护者 🙏

projects.summary: 大家好，我是 Owen Teng，FridayOS 的参与者。这次想自荐一个开源的个人知识管理实践：FridayOS 1.0。 这个项目想解决的问题是：原始资料、正在推进的任务、已经形成的认识和可复用的方法容易混在一起。项目用“六脑方法”把它们分工，再通过来源与反馈联系起来： | 区域 | 负责什么 | |---|---| | inbox | 接住新材料与想法 | | exec | 记录目标、进展和下一步 | | wiki | 积累有来源、可复用的知识 | | skills | 保存经过检验的重复做法 | | raw | 保留原始依据 | | system | 写清规则与 AI 的操作边界 | 这次公开的材料包括： 完整离线蓝图部署包：生成 Markdown 目录、规则与空白模板，支持预览、创建和检查。 可在 Obsidian 打开的中文虚构公司示例，附 11 个练习提示词。 中英文方法与部署教程，代码采用 MIT 许可。 中文介绍 · 部署步骤和下载入口 蓝图部署只需 Python 3.9+，下载后可离线运行；AI 模型和插件需要另行配置。当前部署验收基于 Windows，其他系统、AI 接入和真实使用成效仍需单独验证。“六脑”是组织知识的设计类比，不是脑科学效果主张。 希望它能帮助正在尝试本地知识库或 AI 第二大脑的读者。也欢迎反馈：从下载到第一次整理材料，哪一步最难理解？

projects.title: Rim：一个非稳定类 git 版本管理工具
projects.author: grandlq
projects.summary: - 想要用 AI 提效，却面临自己写好的设计被 AI 改烂、或 slop code 塞满 commit history 的担忧？ - 只是想测试不同的可能性，却不得不创建新 branch 挤满 list ？ - 想要用 agent 简单看看不同方向做出来什么样，但每个方向都要单独建一个 workspace ，最后管理与记住文件夹花费的精力比真正审核代码还多？ 那么，rim 或许适合你。 它是介于 git 与 agent 之间的轻量中间层基础设施，基于 AI 时代「非稳定代码比例持续增加」的理念，不将每一个文件修改都当成高价值、需要完整追溯的 commitment ，而以节点、分叉为版本追溯核心。 使用 rim ，你可以： - 让几个 AI 同时生成不同可能方案，在完成后自己或用 AI 对比验收 - 测试多个方向，选定某个方向后一键剪枝，不留垃圾 - 让 git commit 真正回归只追溯重要与稳定更改，而非留下大量低价值 history - 让 git branch 记录重要的任务分支，而非不断来回切换、塞满每一个细枝末节的并行方向测试 它就在你与下一个 commit 之间。 https://github.com/nekoium/rim Rim 正在 alpha 版本测试中，欢迎试用和 feedback （需求、体验和项目方向都欢迎）。

projects.title: 做了一个 AI 脸龄小工具 FAHR FACE：想看看照片里的自己，如何被 AI 理解
projects.author: fusheng0304
projects.summary: 大家好，最近做了一个小项目 FAHR FACE ，输入一张本人的人像照片，让模型估算照片中的人看起来大约几岁。 地址： https://fahrface.org/zh 想在分享创造聊聊这个项目的背景，以及它后面还能怎么玩。 我们看老照片时，经常会觉得「那时候看起来好青涩」，也会遇到明明隔了没几天，两张照片却像差了好几岁的情况。这里面有时间留下的变化，也有光线、角度和表情造成的差别。如果换成 AI 来看，它会怎样理解同一张脸？这是这个项目想探索的问题。 面部年龄估计这个方向本身并不新鲜，已有公开模型和研究。做这个网站的想法，是把模型能力接成一个普通人也能用的网页：不用配置 Python 环境，不用下载权重，选照片、确认提交，再看到自己的结果。现在使用的是部署在 Hugging Face 上的 FAHR-FaceAge 模型；模型来自已有工作，网站的上传、任务处理、账号与历史记录由这个项目串起来。 我觉得有意思的地方，还在于把几次结果放在一起看。比如找出自己成年后不同时期的照片，看看模型眼里的年龄变化；或者在相近的时间，用不同光线和表情拍摄，观察它究竟有多容易受拍照条件影响。这样既是在看自己的照片，也是在观察一个 AI 模型怎样做判断。结果有时可能更能说明「照片拍成了什么样」，这本身也挺值得琢磨。 目前已经做好的部分比较简单： - 选择 JPG 、PNG 或 WebP 人像，在浏览器本地预览，主动提交后才发送处理。 - 调用模型生成外观年龄估计，在页面查看任务状态和结果。 - 在自己的账号里保存估计结果与测试记录，方便之后回来对照。 - 提供中文界面，以及模型背景、使用方法和隐私说明。 产品上有个想坚持的边界：不给一个看起来精确的数字附加过多含义。这里估算的是照片中的外观年龄，不是生物年龄、健康评分或寿命预测；也不保证每次结果都准确。网站是独立项目，与哈佛或 Mass General Brigham 没有隶属关系。 照片隐私也做了明确说明：预览阶段不上传；提交后会经服务器送到 Hugging Face 上的模型服务处理。自有数据库不保存原始人像，会保存估计结果和任务记录，托管平台的数据处理仍受其政策约束。当前仅面向成年用户使用本人照片。 下一步想探索的是更好用的对比体验，比如给每条记录补上照片拍摄时间、拍摄条件，再整理成个人时间线。这些目前还是想法，现阶段提供的是逐次测试和历史记录。也想看看能不能把「哪些条件会影响估计」说明得更直观，让人知道该怎样理解结果。 想听听 V 友的看法：你会更想拿它看过去几年照片里的变化，还是对比同一时期不同照片的差异？如果给这种工具加一个功能，你最希望是什么？也欢迎直接吐槽这个方向有没有必要继续做。

projects.title: Show HN: A fantasy map of my blog to replace the chronological feed
projects.author: mrcgnc
projects.summary: This is my blog drawn as a network, with a light coat of paint to make it look like a video game map. Each city is a post, bigger cities have more incoming links, and roads are connections between posts. It updates semi-automatically every time I publish. (I used an LLM to write the code and drew about 90% of the art myself in Inkscape.) For a long time I've been unsatisfied with the linear feeds and tag soups that most blogs use, so I decided to experiment with a non-linear view. I built some CLI tools that combine embedding similarity, LLM suggestions and human review to find the links between posts and quantify their strength. Now, every time I write a new piece, it takes me about 5 minutes to generate its links to/from older posts and grow the map accordingly. The map is meant to look playful more than precise. For me, the key feature is how it enables making your own "journey" through the blog. The tricky part was finding a layout where closely related posts end up near each other AND the landscape doesn't change dramatically with every new post. I'm not a graph expert, but t-SNE on shortest-path distances over the link graph turned out to work well in my tests. Each update starts from the previous positions with early exaggeration off, and a Procrustes alignment keeps the map from rotating or drifting. I hope it helps people get lost in there and find things they want to read. I'd like to see something like this on other blogs, so I'm sharing it here. I wonder if anyone else has tried similar ways to un-linearize their blogs.

projects.author: cryptostrapon

github.name: cryptostrapon/npm-install-audit
github.description: Zero dependency Node script that flags install hooks and risky code in a repo before you run npm install. For take-home tests and unknown projects.

projects.summary: Project URL Category JS Project Title A zero dependency Node script that flags install hooks and risky code in a repo before your first npm install Project Description Run it on a repo you did not write, like a take-home test from a recruiter, before npm install. It lists preinstall, install, postinstall and prepare hooks and flags shell execution, runtime base64 decoding, curl pipes and credential paths. Highlights One file, no dependencies, no network access, read only: it never runs the code it checks. Built for a real attack: fake recruiter take-home repos that hide the payload in an install hook. Clear exit codes (1 flagged, 0 clean, 2 unreadable) and a self test, easy to drop into CI. Honest about limits: a clean result is not proof of safety, and the README says what it cannot catch. MIT licensed. Good first issues are open (JSON output, TypeScript files, git URL dependencies). Example Code markdown curl -O node audit.js ./take-home-task ! package.json: postinstall hook runs: node scripts/setup.js ! scripts/setup.js: runs shell commands ! scripts/setup.js: decodes base64 at runtime ! scripts/setup.js: pipes a download into a shell 4 finding(s). Read them before you run npm install. Screenshots or Demo Videos

github.description: 轻量的 Windows 桌面悬浮监控：电池功耗与续航、CPU/GPU/内存占用与功耗、网速、真实延迟与断网提醒。原生 C++ / Direct2D，迷你模式约 0.1% CPU。

projects.summary: 笔记本现在耗电多少瓦、剩下的电还能用多久、网络是真断了还是只是慢？Pulse 把这些信息放在桌面的一张小卡片上，随时可见。它用原生 C++ 和 Direct2D 编写，单个 exe 免安装，支持 Windows 10 / 11。 主要功能： 功耗与续航：读取 Windows 自带的 RAPL 能耗计数器，显示处理器、CPU、核显、内存的功耗；用电池时给出平滑后的续航预计和到 20% 的剩余时间。无需管理员权限。 真实网络延迟：用 HTTP 请求测延迟并判定断网，走系统代理，所以在 Clash TUN 这类 ping 总显示 0 ms 的环境下也准确；断网和恢复时弹出提醒卡片。 两种显示模式：完整卡片和迷你单行，双击切换，各自显示哪些指标都能在右键菜单里勾选。 迷你模式自身只占单核约 0.1%–0.3%，只采集勾选的指标。程序只读取系统计数器，不改系统设置，联网仅用于测延迟，没有统计和自动更新。发布包由 GitHub Actions 从源码构建，采用 MIT 许可证。

projects.title: [开源推荐] 王者万象棋对局助手：按开局选择重算阵容榜，去掉幸存者偏差（作者自荐）

projects.title: Show HN: ReviewerAgent and StopContinue, for CC and Codex with Pi
projects.author: raylad
projects.summary: This package is designed to solve two problems: 1. Frontier models like Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Astra 6.0 and Sol 6.1 all make errors and bugs that can be found by another model (even a much smaller model like Luna). 2. In what is supposed to be a long development run, for example against a plan, models will decide to stop before they are finished, when there is obviously more work to do, or to ask a question they already should know the answer to. ReviewerAgent blocks git commits and sends them to another agent that reviews the staged files and either allows the commit or returns a list of issues to fix. StopContinue evaluates every agent stop and determines if it still has work to do or if it is asking a question that it has the answer to already. In either of those cases, it prompts the agent to keep working and specifies next steps or answers to questions, based on the current plan document and chat history. The system works for and is tested on Claude Code and Codex as the developer harness, and either of those or any other model, through Pi, as the reviewer. I've developed it over the last 4 months or so and used it daily over that period. Take a look if it sounds useful. It's been tested on MacOS and Linux (Ubuntu), and has agent assisted install, update, and removal scripts, for convenience. Stats: Over four months of daily use of the system while developing it (from late June til today), reviewerAgent (usually a GPT Luna model) gated 3,877 commits, running about 7,600 reviews in total, so about half of those commits were rejected at least once. The coding agent (Fable or Opus) almost never disagreed with the reviewer's judgements: over the last month, for example, it pushed back on just 3 of 693 rejections. Each rejection listed an average of two required fixes and most rejected commits were accepted after a second round (90% within five attempts). Rejection rates increased with commit size: only 23% of code commits under 50 lines were sent back, but 72% of those over 1,000 lines were initially rejected. Here's an example of a bug that it caught last month for me. More examples in the README: The Fable 5.1 developer agent wrote a wrapper script that runs a set of R validation checks against a freshly loaded database and records whether each one passed. (One of two required fixes shown.) REQUIRED FIXES (blocking) 2. docs/database-phase-loader/local-load/run_r_checks.sh:4-6 pipes each R check through tail without pipefail or explicit status handling, so a failed Rscript can still produce a zero exit status and be recorded as successful. Preserve and propagate each check's exit status. In a shell pipeline the exit status is that of the last command, so `Rscript check.R | tail` reports `tail`'s success even when the check fails. The script prints the tail of the failing check's output, exits 0, and records a pass. A broken load would have been certified as validated.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Treefold：把 AI Coding 的多仓库、Worktree、终端和任务放在一起
projects.author: win5do

github.name: win5do/treefold
github.description: A local-first macOS app for running AI agents in parallel Git worktrees. Keep code, terminals, and tasks together, then merge changes back cleanly.

projects.summary: LLM 时代高强度用 AI Agent 搞项目，LLM 很强，但想要高效舒服的开发还是有很多繁琐的流程。 例如经常同时推进几个任务，还涉及前后端两个 repo，并行任务不相互冲突大家都知道用 git worktree。 手敲 git worktree 命令很繁琐，AI 可以代劳，但每次都要交代一遍却挺烦：从哪个分支创建，前后端项目在哪个目录，做完合回哪里。想去对应目录跑条命令，还得找路径、开终端、切过去。任务一多，就容易忘记哪个目录对应哪件事。 我就在想能不能把常用流程做到一个 ui 界面中管理，于是做了一个 APP 叫 Treefold。我想把每项任务的代码、终端和进度放在一起，打开就知道做到哪了，接下来可以继续做什么。 任务展开以后，要知道怎么收回来 我把工作分成三层：Project、Workspace、Fork。 Project 放一个项目相关的仓库和目录。我一般让原仓库保持在 main 分支，再为每项 feature 创建 Workspace，各自使用独立分支和 worktree。创建时默认从原仓库当前分支展开，也可以选择其他本地或远端分支作为起点。 一个 feature 里有可以并行的子任务，就继续创建 Fork。比如做“商品搜索”，可以让几个 Fork 分别负责接口、页面和测试，各自在独立目录里修改，完成后合回父 Workspace，再一起联调和交付。 这样，worktree 就有了明确的父子关系，交付时知道应该合回哪里。操作由人确认，发生冲突仍然需要处理。Workspace 还可以选择推送 feature 分支，接着走原来的远端评审流程。 简单任务开一个 Workspace 就够了，不用每次都拆 Fork。同一 Workspace 里的多个 Session 共享代码目录；需要隔离修改时，再创建 Fork。 worktree 多了，目录和状态都得看得清 git worktree list 能列出目录和分支，但想知道里面是否有未提交的修改、改动是否已经合回去，还得逐个检查。任务多了，这些小操作也会打断思路。 Treefold 把 worktree list 做成了界面里的管理列表，按仓库展开。每个 worktree 的分支、路径、当前提交和关联任务放在一起，同时显示未提交改动、冲突，以及相对目标分支领先或落后的提交数。已经合入目标分支的状态也会标出来，不用挨个进入目录查 Git。 从列表可以直接打开关联任务；不再使用的 worktree，可以在界面里确认后删除，也能清理失效的 worktree 记录。哪些还在开发、哪些改动已经合入、哪些目录可以收拾，都有地方查看。 完成的任务可以归档，先保留分支、worktree 和工作记录，之后再按需清理。Project 里可以批量清理已归档的 Workspace，Workspace 里也能清理已归档的 Fork。隔天回来看时，活跃任务和已完成的工作分开，也能找到之前的交付记录。 创建 worktree、启动 Session 和批量清理都可以在后台继续，不用一直守着弹窗。切去做其他任务后，也能回来查看状态和失败原因。 Agent 写完，检查代码和提交 我一直挺喜欢 JetBrains 的 Git 集成：修改在哪里，提交了什么，都可以直接看。 Treefold 里也放了 Git Changes 和 History。开发过程中看 diff，交付前检查提交；几个零散提交可以用 Squash 整理成一个，也可以 Reset 到指定提交。当前分支最新一次提交的说明写得不合适，也可以直接在 History 里修改。如果本地记录显示它被远端分支、标签或其他分支引用，会先提醒，再由我决定是否继续。 完成交付时，可以选择 Squash，把这项工作的成果合成一个提交放进父分支。前后端改动不一样，就分别填写提交说明，在同一个弹窗里检查后一起确认。源分支上的开发记录仍然保留，父分支收到的是整理后的提交。 我没有做完整的交互式 rebase 和冲突编辑器。常用操作放在界面里，更复杂的 Git 操作继续交给终端和 Agent，处理完再回来检查结果。 Project 里也能直接查看和搜索本地、远端分支，切换分支，或者删除不再需要的分支。这些短操作，不用每次都通过聊天交给 Agent。 检查代码时，也不想每次都重新告诉 Agent：“这是哪几个仓库，应该和哪个分支比较，别漏掉还没提交的修改。”所以加了 AI Review：在 Workspace 或 Fork 里选一个 Agent，确认提示词，就会打开一个专门检查这项工作的 Session。 Fork 和父 Workspace 比较，Workspace 和 Project 当前分支比较。Treefold 会把各仓库的路径、分支和比较范围交给 Agent，要求同时检查已提交、未提交的修改和新文件。默认提示词让它先报告问题，我确认后，可以在同一个 Session 里继续讨论、修复和验证。也可以给 Project 保存自己的 Review 提示词。 这样，从开发、检查到修复都留在同一项任务里，最后再决定怎么交付。完成交付前，如果还有将被停止的 Session 在运行，界面会先列出来，让我选择暂缓交付，或者确认停止后继续。这里检查的是进程是否还活着，不能替我判断 Agent 是否已经做完。 暂缓的任务，先记在 Todo 里 和 AI 讨论方案时，经常会冒出一些现在不做、以后值得试的点子。以前我会开个文件记 Todo，接下来还得记得这个文件放在哪。 现在可以直接记到 Workspace 的 Todo list。要做的时候，把 Todo 分配给 Fork，展开成一项独立工作；完成并合回父 Workspace 后，关联的 Todo 也会完成。 Treefold 也带了 CLI 和 Skill，Agent 能读取、添加和修改 Todo，遇到问题时也能记录阻塞原因。换一个 Session 接着做，代码、Todo 和交付记录都还留在 Workspace 里，不用依赖某一次聊天记住所有事情。 比如接口开发时发现一个值得单独处理的问题，可以先留下 Todo，继续完成手头的工作。等有空了再把它分出去，也不用为了保留这个点子一直开着原来的 Session。 Agent 把服务跑起来了，我却看不到它在干什么 调试的时候，我经常要让 Agent 启动前后端服务。以前它通常在自己的会话后台启动，再告诉我“服务已经起来了”。我只知道启动了，眼前却没有一个能持续看日志的终端。想知道请求有没有进来、服务有没有报错，还得让它再查一遍。 两个 Agent 并行工作时更麻烦：各自的会话没有共享的进程列表，不知道对方已经启动了什么。一个刚把服务跑起来，另一个又启动一遍，端口就冲突了。 Treefold 用 amux 管理这些需要持续运行的进程。服务可以跟着任务列出来，人能在界面里看日志、输入命令，Agent 也能通过 amux 查询进程、读取日志、停止或重启服务。几个 Session 可以共同观察同一个服务，启动前先查看已有进程，再决定复用还是另开一套。 切走页面不影响进程运行，也不用再回忆服务藏在哪次聊天里。不过并行启动多套服务时，端口仍然需要分别配置，Treefold 目前不会自动隔离端口。 关闭窗口时，可以选择让 App 留在后台，或者直接退出。退出 App 后是否保留 amux 和受管进程，则由单独的设置控制。 一个任务，可能要改几个仓库 有些项目的前后端是两个 Git 仓库。一个功能要两边一起改，就得告诉 AI 两边的位置，同步创建分支和 worktree，再检查是不是进了对应的目录。 所以 Treefold 的一个 Project 可以放多个仓库。创建 Workspace 或 Fork 时，相关仓库一起准备分支和 worktree，后续查看修改、同步和交付也在同一个任务里完成，各仓库的结果分别展示。 接手已有工作也不用从头开始。创建 Workspace 时，每个仓库可以分别新建分支，或者选一个已有的本地或远端分支继续做。分支列表可以搜索，已经被其他 worktree 占用的本地分支会标出来，避免选错工作目录。前端从 main 开始，后端接着已有 feature 开发，也可以放进同一个 Workspace。 还有 monorepo：一个仓库里放了很多项目，我可能只关心其中几个目录。Treefold 可以把这些子目录设为工作入口，也可以加入外部资料目录，方便 Agent 找到相关上下文。目录选择帮助组织工作，Git worktree 仍然以整个仓库为单位。 需要换回熟悉的工具时，Open With 可以直接在 IDE、终端或 Finder 中打开当前目录，也能一键复制路径。选中了哪个任务，就打开它对应的工作目录。 保留终端习惯，少记几个快捷键 我日常主要用 Agent 的 CLI 和 TUI，所以 Treefold 里的 Agent 也是原来的终端界面。目前支持 Codex、Claude Code、OpenCode 和 Pi，也可以单独开 Shell 跑命令。终端使用 xterm.js。 Agent 使用本机安装的 CLI，沿用自己的登录和模型配置。喜欢哪个就用哪个，同一项任务里也可以开不同的 Agent Session。使用前先确认相应 CLI 在终端里能正常运行；没有配置 Agent，也可以先用 Shell。 我喜欢 Command Palette，但不想记一大堆快捷键。所以默认只给少数高频操作绑定快捷键，其他操作从 Palette 找，也可以按自己的习惯修改绑定。 这里我比较在意上下文：在某个 Fork 里打开 Palette，新建 Session、开始 AI Review 或打开目录，就应该接着使用这个 Fork 的上下文，不用重新选一遍。 免费开源，本地运行 Treefold 免费开源，使用 AGPL-3.0-only 许可证。App 在本机运行，项目状态、任务、Session 元数据和配置保存在自己的电脑上，核心管理功能不依赖云端服务。 Agent 沿用你自己的模型和服务配置，模型调用、网络访问和费用由对应服务及配置决定。目前支持 Apple Silicon Mac，需要 macOS 14 或更新版本。

projects.summary: Since Railway getting pwned is getting all the attention right now, I thought now is a good time to showcase what we've been building. Stackdome is a self hosted platform as a service. The idea is to have simplicity of platforms like Railway and Render, but with the ability to run everything on infrastructure you control. With Stackdome, you can deploy an application from GitHub, connect multiple services visually, add a managed database, create preview environments, and roll back the entire application if a release breaks. Features: - First class support for multi-service applications, shown on a canvas in the UI (inspired by Railway). You can edit, wire up, and create resources from the canvas. - First class support for multiple clusters. Stackdome acts as the hub and places workloads across clusters (hub and spoke). - Self hostable, from a small VPS to a large k8s cluster. - Managed Postgres with WAL archiving, HA, backups, and PITR (CNPG underneath). - A release system for the whole stack. A release targets everything, and you can roll it back if something breaks. - Source to image, with an in cluster registry (Zot). - Disposable preview environments, which can also be multi-service. - Declarative apps via a Stackfile, deployed with the CLI. Basically, the idea is to package the tooling in the CNCF/cloud-native ecosystem into an opinionated platform, so that developers can get a without being an expert in Kubernetes or a dozen other projects from the CNCF landscape. projects.title: Show HN: TUI to manage firewall and HTTP server, in Rust
projects.author: FabCH
projects.summary: I have been self-hosting for 10 years, and "family hosting" for 2. The number of attacks my servers get has increased by 3x since May of this year. Now personally, I don't like hiding behind Cloudflare because I don't want them to be a SPOF, but it was becoming a bit too scary to just be open to the web. Because it is a family cloud, it can't hide behind a VPN, it has to support devices like TV sticks that can't connect properly over VPN. It has to support HTTPS. So I put together a Rust/Ratatui TUI+cron/CLI that manages my second line of defense: firewall and HTTP server. I run a reverse Nginx proxy in front of apps like Nextcloud, and a nftables firewall with SSH as my admin tunnel. It does several things: 1) It allows me to block entire segments, countries, datacenter IP ranges, TOR exit nodes etc... 2) It allows me to block specific bots: search bots, AI bots, security scanners 3) It does dynamic blocking too, looking at the logs to spot bad behavior and block it. I used to run fail2ban for SSH for example, but a centralized UI for both SSH and HTTP(S) is nicer IMHO. So if this is useful to anyone else, feel free. It's AGPL v3. In my experience, geoblocking is the biggest win, reducing the attacks by 30x. AI Disclosure: I use AI assisted development. I follow Linus Torvalds and Bob Martin model, with using AI as a tool and verifying the result.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】OpenWrt / VPS 网络排障工具箱：新手诊断入口与真实案例
projects.author: wukai8775-max

github.name: wukai8775-max/openwrt-vps-streaming-diagnostics
github.description: OpenWrt / Xray / VPS network troubleshooting · 网络慢与直播卡顿排障：只读快照、受限测试、脱敏案例、验收与回滚。

projects.summary: 你好，自荐一个采用 MIT 许可证的开源项目：OpenWrt / VPS 网络诊断工具箱。 它来自我们排查“Wi-Fi 能连，网站却打不开”“下载有速度，任务仍然超时”“负载下响应变慢”的实际过程。最近精简了首页，补上新手诊断入口和结果示例，希望让第一次排查网络问题的人先看懂报告，再决定查哪一层。 项目首页 新手诊断入口 结果示例 真实案例索引 新手可以先做什么 安装 Python 3.10+ 后，运行 python3 tools/quick-check.py，默认只显示离线合成演示，不联网，也不用提供路由器密码或服务器账号。 明确加上 --execute 后，才使用 curl 8.4+ 执行最多三次 IPv4 HTTPS 轻量请求，每次最多五秒、响应体预算 64 KiB，默认不下载测速文件，不自动修改网络配置。当前指南面向 macOS / Linux。 中文报告和 JSON 来自同一份结果，分别记录完整、失败和未开始次数。部分下载不会算成成功吞吐；入门报告不输出真实地址、接口名、凭据、响应正文或原始错误。 两个真实的脱敏排障案例 1. 下载收到约 97.6%，仍然记录为失败。 一笔固定 10 MiB 对象请求获得 HTTP 200、收到大部分数据，却没在 20 秒预算内完整结束，照样记为部分超时。后续原配置短测完成，只记录“本轮未复现”，没有宣称旧问题修复。下载超时复查 2. 某个目标更快，另一目标性能复核未通过，最终回滚。 一项接收缓存候选让部分下载变快，但另一固定对象的重复测试未达到预设性能保留门槛，因此恢复原值。另一目标在两种条件下都完整下载，未通过的是性能门槛；正向、负向结果和回滚决定全部保留。缓存实验与恢复记录 进阶资料还包括只读采集、受时间和流量预算约束的固定对象上下行测试、单项实验卡、验收与回滚，以及交给其他 Agent 接手的提示词。 小请求通过不代表带宽上限、指定代理节点或手机直播稳定性已经验收；每个环境仍需建立自己的基线。欢迎反馈可复现的工具问题和脱敏测量结果。 说明：作者自荐，投稿文字由 AI 助手协助整理；案例事实已按公开记录核对。

projects.summary: 初见是一款融合圣经名画赏析与经文阅读的中英文学习工具。通过画中的人物、细节和创作背景，认识相关圣经故事，再回到经文中深入阅读。让喜欢艺术的人找到了解圣经的起点，也让读经的人多一种欣赏与理解故事的方式。社区版提供4件馆藏画作、5节入门短课及中英文圣经阅读，免费使用，无需注册。 亮点 看懂圣经名画，读懂画中的圣经故事。 画中的人物是谁？这一刻发生了什么？画家为什么这样描绘？ 初见从这些好奇出发，带你欣赏圣经主题的经典画作，认识画中的人物与故事，了解作品的创作背景，再阅读相关经文。随着故事逐渐清晰，画中的一个眼神、一个手势、一处细节，也会有更多值得留意的意味。 我是项目维护者。无论你是喜欢古典艺术，还是想开始了解圣经，都可以从一幅感兴趣的画开始。中英文导读与入门短课，陪你逐步理解作品，也更深入地阅读圣经。 一幅画，读出两种时代。 在委罗内塞的《发现摩西》中，古埃及的故事被画家以当时的华服和宫廷随从重新呈现。初见把画面观察、创作背景与《出埃及记》第2章放在一起，帮助读者理解原文，也看见艺术家的表达。这个例子有美国国家美术馆藏品说明作为依据。 从“好看”走向“看得懂”。 每件作品都有具体观察提示：跟随人物的目光、寻找手势指向、留意空间如何安排。导读标明经文、历史背景和编辑观察，并提供收藏机构原始页面，方便继续查阅。 让第一次接触的人也有起点。 画作导读和入门短课均可切换中英文。短课用一段阅读、一个问题和答题反馈，帮助用户练习理解上下文。可以从艺术开始，也可以直接阅读经文。 从《发现摩西》开始，认识画中的人，也读懂他们的故事 → 谁发现了河边的婴孩？她为什么决定救下他？一个发生在古埃及的故事，为什么被画家描绘得像文艺复兴时期的宫廷？ 跟着初见观察画面、了解创作背景，再读一读《出埃及记》中的记载。你会接触到故事本身，也能了解画家如何用自己的时代与艺术语言重新呈现它。欢迎分享你留意到的细节。 社区版与开源实现 当前提供4件馆藏画作、5节双语短课，两种经文各含66卷、1,189章，另有设备朗读、本机收藏和备份。采用原生 JavaScript、静态 JSON 与浏览器本地存储，无 npm 依赖或后端，可自行部署 GitHub Pages，不需要 API 密钥。 设备朗读的音色与可用性取决于系统和浏览器；收藏保存在当前浏览器。应用代码采用 MIT 许可，经文、图像与字体分别记录来源和许可。博物馆资料用于出处核对，不代表机构为本应用背书。

projects.title: Show HN: KeibiDrop – Work on remote large files on-demand (no upload/download)
projects.author: coldstartops
projects.summary: We have built KeibiDrop because me and the people close to me were tired of cloud storages, and to copy data fully across our devices in order to use it. Now with KeibiDrop you can mount and stream folders between your computers (and web browser) access and edit data on-demand as if it was local. You can try it instantly in the browser https://web.keibidrop.com/ (you need two devices) or by building from source/ downloading from the github releases. (there are also demo recordings in the Readme on github). We also got a marketing website for it here: https://keibidrop.com The desktop app, engine and CLI are FOSS AGPL-v3 and in terms of architecture and stack the following holds: - It uses a full-duplex P2P IPv6 connection between peers with a fallback to a data forwarding relay. - We got a dual networking stack QUIC + TCP using protocol buffers (WebRTC to be added), and we use ML-KEM-1024 + X25519 for the handshake and either aes-gcm-256 or chacha20-poly1305 for the session, and we do a latency hiding re-key inspired by Signal's SPQR. - it relies on FUSE, macFUSE, and WinFsp as filesystem drivers and the whole gist of it is to "hide the latency" of remote filesystems and to just give the feeling of teleporting files. - we use golang for the engine, and rust + slint.dev for the GUI Our goal was to have a lightweight, cross platform filesystem that does not use many resources, has the RAM usage bounded and gives the feeling as if working on a local filesystem. Currently the filesystem respects POSIX semantics, (except for symlinks and hardlinks, I have them disabled), and we tested it on intercontinental links (between Romania and Singapore), on both relayed connections and direct connections. You can use git, pijul, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or any tools you would normally use on your local computer, or use our docker image on your NAS storage and instantly access the data you need while you are travelling.
