projects.title: [开源自建邮局] 三叶草邮局发布！操作傻瓜化、配置可视化，同时管理 N 个邮箱， 5 分钟三步开邮局
projects.author: T800ai
projects.summary: # clover 三叶草邮局 🍀 项目地址： https://github.com/Vincentkeio/clover-mail 在自己的服务器上搭建邮件服务，通过 Web 面板管理域名、邮箱和转发规则。 ## 三步开邮局： 1.接入 cloudflare token; 2.面板一键安装邮件服务器 TLS ； 3.点击创建邮箱。 ## 全程可视化，傻瓜配置，5 分钟创建强大易用的个人邮局。 ## 功能特色 - **可视化管理**：集中管理多个域名、邮箱账户、密码和邮件转发，支持别名、前缀匹配与 Catch-all 。 - **Cloudflare DNS 自动配置**：导入域名，一键生成并推送 MX 、SPF 、DKIM 、DMARC 等邮件记录，也可导出后手动配置。 - **Roundcube Webmail**：从面板选择邮箱，在新标签页免密进入；使用原生搜索、星标、文件夹、编辑器和通讯录。 - **兼容邮件客户端**：支持 IMAP 、POP3 、SMTP 和 ManageSieve ，可使用 Thunderbird 、Foxmail 、Apple Mail 等客户端。 - **全局邮箱设置**：统一管理协议开关、远程图片策略及附件上限；附件默认 100 MB ，可设置为无限额。 - **证书与运维**：支持 HTTPS 、邮件 TLS 证书管理和自动续期，提供环境检查、反垃圾统计、邮件队列、日志及备份入口。 - **账户安全与 API**：单管理员管理，支持两步验证、Passkey 、API Token 和审计日志。 ## 安装准备 - Debian 11–13 或 Ubuntu 22.04+ 服务器；默认发布镜像支持 **amd64**。 - 最低配置：**1 vCPU 、2 GB 内存**；推荐配置：**2 vCPU 、4 GB 内存**。 - 准备一个面板域名和邮件域名，将面板域名的 A 记录指向服务器公网 IP 。 - 公网开放 **80 、443 、25**；邮件客户端按需开放 **465 、587 、993**，POP3S 使用 **995**。 - 确认服务器提供商允许邮件收发，并支持设置 PTR/rDNS 。 安装器可安装 Docker ；已有受支持的宿主机 Caddy 或 Nginx 时，可共享 Web 入口。 ## 快速安装 推荐使用一键安装： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vincentkeio/clover-mail/main/bootstrap.sh -o /tmp/clover-bootstrap.sh bash /tmp/clover-bootstrap.sh ``` 也可克隆仓库后安装： ```bash git clone https://github.com/Vincentkeio/clover-mail.git clover cd clover bash install.sh ``` 按提示填写面板域名。首次安装会在终端显示随机生成的管理员账号和密码，请保存后登录面板。 ### Docker Compose 安装 适合已安装 Docker 和 Compose v2 、可独占 80/443 等所需端口的 Linux 服务器。以 root 在服务器操作： ```bash git clone https://github.com/Vincentkeio/clover-mail.git clover cd clover cp .env.example .env nano .env ``` 将 `PANEL_HOSTNAME`、`MAIL_DOMAIN`、`MAIL_HOSTNAME` 和 `ACME_EMAIL` 改为自己的域名和邮箱；可同时填写 `CLOVER_VPS_IP`、调整时区及其他参数。首次安装的密钥项保留模板值或留空即可，初始化会自动生成。 保存后运行一条命令完成安装： ```bash CLOVER_HOME="$PWD" docker compose --profile install run --rm installer ``` Compose 初始化会生成密钥、准备邮件 TLS 、启动服务、创建管理员并安装 `clover` 快捷命令。管理员凭据显示在终端；已有数据和管理员会保留。后续可直接用 `docker compose up -d` 启动服务。已有宿主机 Nginx/Caddy 需共享端口时，请使用上方推荐的安装器。 ## 开始使用 1. **环境配置**：连接 Cloudflare ，选择邮件域名并设置邮件主机名，生成和推送 DNS 记录。 2. **检查环境**：检查 DNS 、端口及 TLS 证书；为邮件主机申请证书，并在服务器提供商处设置 PTR/rDNS 。 3. **邮箱账户**：创建邮箱及密码；需要转发时，在“别名与转发”中添加规则。 4. **Webmail**：选择邮箱并点击“进入 Roundcube”，或按[客户端配置指南](docs/mail-client-setup.md)连接邮件客户端。 Cloudflare Token 需要目标域名的区域读取及 DNS 编辑权限。邮件主机的 A 记录应设为 **DNS only**。 首次邮件证书可能为自签证书，请在连接客户端前申请可信证书。邮件能否送达还取决于服务器 IP 信誉、PTR 和收件方策略。 ## 更新与日常管理 在服务器输入 `clover` 打开管理菜单，或直接运行： ```bash clover status # 查看服务状态 clover update # 更新 clover logs # 查看日志 clover backup # 备份面板数据库与邮件配置 clover admin list # 查看管理员 ``` 更新会保留配置和 Docker 数据卷。 管理员密码遗失时，在服务器运行 `clover admin reset `。 ## 数据与安全 - 邮件与配置保存在服务器的 Docker 数据卷中； Roundcube 的通讯录和偏好独立保存。 - `.env` 含服务密钥，请妥善保管，不要公开上传。 - 面板仅有一个管理员；免密 Webmail 入口允许管理员进入所选邮箱。 ## 许可证 Clover 采用 AGPL-3.0-or-later ，具体条款及来源声明见仓库中的 LICENSE 和 NOTICE 。 Roundcube 、docker-mailserver 等第三方组件遵循各自的开源许可证。 ![image]( https://cdn.nodeimage.com/i/aPVbJabKDjUOK2jScFiTo0K5msQ9Frqb.png) ![image]( https://cdn.nodeimage.com/i/NFxyIpo9MZAmZx9k5xZPZ6nWYEKqROV9.png)

projects.summary: Let me begin by explaining what it is: SchemaWright is a platform for learning database table design in a gamified way, with a real Postgres database running on your browser via WASM. It was heavily inspired by Duolingo and LeetCode, because I love the way how those platforms teach their users. I built and launched this a couple months ago, weeks after my first SaaS failed (that one was called NoteRaven, and the idea was for it to be a Notion + Medium + Udemy all in one platform; but after looking at how saturated that market was, I decided to move on). The story on how I came up with it is basically that I was working normally on my day job, and noticed how many times we had changed some core tables, and usually discussed renaming them, changing columns, relationships etc. After that, I realized that I wanted to learn how to "get the schema right" from the beginning, so I began looking for websites that could teach that. It didnt take long to realize I couldn't find one that fitted my needs: it had to feel gamified and rigorous at the same time. When I say "rigorous" I mean that the content shouldnt be standard exercises we see in university (that we never really use at work) or loose definitions we feel like is too shallow. Therefore, I decided that I would be the one to build such platform. The way I structured the app is by separating it in 3 main pages: Learn, Exercises and Lectures. The first one is where you'll find Duolingo like lessons for database schema, it goes from the foundations (what is a table, what are rows and columns), to intermediate/advanced contents, such as concurrency and queues, scaling and architecture etc. It has 8 levels, but I currently only wrote up to level 3 (normalisation). Which is funny because my boss once tested me on this lol. The Exercises page is where I took inspiratoin from LeetCode, especially the page for an exercise structure: on the left side you have the problem description, your submissions and an editorial, and on the right side the code editor and the tests that will run on your code. Finally the last page is for people who are keen on reading papers and are more drawn to academic research. The lectures reference famous and important research papers that led us to our current understanding of databases, sql and concepts we learn today on this subject. It summarizes them and teaches you the concepts, while containing some interactive exercises too! Ok, so why do I think this may work as opposed to NoteRaven? One of the reasons is that I shared this with my co-workers (60+ people, most are devs too) and boss (who is CEO and CTO), and they really enjoyed using it. That same boss gave me positive feedback and suggestions, that I actually ended up implementing on the platform (yeah your suggestion could end up there too!). Another would be that I feel like platforms that train you on database design are scarce compared to ones that teach you queries, so the market wouldn't be so saturated. Let me know what you guys think! Please share if you think some exercises are unfair, meaning that they need better context for people to answer them, and also what you think of the lesson's pace, content and interactive exercises; the same goes for the lectures.

projects.summary: I never felt comfortable signing up for cloud budgeting apps and having them store all of my financial data on their servers. I also didn't find locally hosted options that I liked using. That led me to build Maali ( https://maali.app ) over the past year. It is currently a Mac and Windows app that lets you track spending, budgets, recurring bills, income, net worth, and more. It stores all of your data on your computer. You can bring your data in by either manually importing bank statement files (CSV/PDF), or by using SimpleFIN, a third-party bridge that you set up once and it keeps your data in sync. Since SimpleFIN introduces a third party that moves your data, I also added a power-user feature where Maali watches a folder (per account) and imports files dropped there, so you can automate downloads however you like and keep everything local. It also has an optional AI analyst (local Gemma 4 E4B model) that provides commentary on your spending and flags anything unusual about your finances. I realize that mobile is a big part of convenience for people. Maali lets you set up a phone web app over your own Tailscale network, paired by QR code. I'm also close to launching iOS/Android mobile apps that keep data in sync between the desktop/mobile apps using end-to-end encryption. My goal is to provide a great user experience with maximum convenience without sacrificing privacy. The full app is free to use for 30 days (no card/signup needed). After that, if you find it useful and want to continue using it, it's $99 one-time. There's a live demo on the site ( https://maali.app/today ) with synthetic data so you can get a feel for it. Would love to hear any feedback that you have.

projects.title: Analyse-Trading
projects.summary: Analyse-Trading is a social network built only for traders. Publish signals with entry, stop loss and take profit: every closed signal is added to your public track record. Connect MT4/MT5, cTrader or TradeLocker to share your trades automatically, or copy traders whose results you trust. Join public or private communities, enter trading challenges and follow live market news. Free on web, iPhone and Android, in English, French, Spanish, Italian and German.

projects.title: Show HN: Vibetown – public sandboxes to vibecode with strangers
projects.author: nickmarch31
projects.summary: Vibetown is a site where you can create a public sandbox (shoutout fly.io sprites / machines) that anyone can contribute to with their AI agents. You can also get matched with a random person in a sandbox to vibe code with them, and if you like what you built then you can open it up and keep it running! Think of it something like twitch meets lovable. There is a chat in each room, along with a localhost preview. People take turns connecting their Claude Code subscriptions and making any changes to the app. Sandboxes automatically go to sleep after a while, but can be woken up. It's completely free because right now I'm only supporting frontend apps. Use it to create art or cool websites without anything fancy. In the future, I will add database, AI (api), and other integrations. The short-term goal is just to see how people collaborate with strangers on public apps. The long-term goal is to make it possible for indie devs to build fully working apps with others that actually generate revenue. Let me know what you think! I have 4 public sandboxes running right now that anyone can hop in and contribute to.

projects.title: QuotaPanel：基于 Wails 的 AI 订阅额度管理工具
projects.author: ModStart
projects.summary: # 引言 在 AI 开发日益普及的今天，开发者需要同时管理 Claude 、ChatGPT 、GitHub Copilot 、Kimi 等多个平台的订阅与 API 额度。这些额度信息分散在各个控制台，难以快速掌握整体使用情况。 **QuotaPanel** 是一款开源的桌面端 AI 额度管理工具，基于 **Go + Wails + Vue3** 技术栈开发，支持 16 种 AI 订阅与 API 额度来源，本地优先保护隐私，跨平台支持 macOS/Windows/Linux 。 ![]( https://open-cdn.tecmz.com/theme/apps/quotapanel/images/account.png?t=202609261508) ## 核心特性 ### 本地优先设计 QuotaPanel 采用**本地优先**架构，所有账号密钥与浏览器会话数据均保存在本机（默认 `~/.quotapanel/`），不会上传到云端。数据目录支持通过 `QUOTAPANEL_DATA_ROOT` 环境变量自定义位置。 ### 多源额度聚合 工具支持 16 种 AI 订阅与 API 额度来源，分为两大类： **浏览器登录类**： - Claude 订阅（ 5 小时及每周额度） - ChatGPT/Codex （订阅使用窗口） - Cursor （当前周期用量） - Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan （套餐积分与账户余额） **API Key 类**： - GitHub Copilot （ Premium 、聊天与补全额度） - Z.ai Coding Plan 、Kimi Coding Plan 、MiniMax Token Plan - Devin/Windsurf 、Grok CLI 、OpenCode - Command Goat 、DeepSeek API 、Kimi API - OpenRouter 、OpenAI API ### 额度可视化 通过进度条、余额明细、账期/重置时间等可视化元素，系统提供正常、即将用尽、超限三档状态色，超出阈值时会主动提示。 ![]( https://open-cdn.tecmz.com/theme/apps/quotapanel/images/account-dark.png?t=202609261508) ## 技术架构 ### 技术栈 - **Go 1.24+**：后端核心逻辑与额度查询服务 - **Wails v2**：跨平台桌面应用框架 - **Vue3 + TypeScript**：前端界面开发 - **AntDesign Vue**：UI 组件库 - **TailwindCSS**：样式框架 - **SQLite**：本地数据存储 ### 项目结构 ``` quotapanel/ ├── main.go # Wails 应用配置与入口 ├── app*.go # App 暴露给前端的方法 ├── backend/ │ ├── base/ # 基础库（数据库、配置、日志、窗口、平台差异等） │ └── quota/ # 各额度供应商适配器与查询服务 ├── frontend/ │ └── packages/ │ ├── ui/ # 主界面（ Vue3 + AntDesignVue + TailwindCSS ） │ └── quota/ # 额度业务模块 ├── demo/image/ # 界面截图 ├── docs/ # 文档（额度来源调研等） └── Makefile # 开发、构建与发布命令 ``` ### 开发环境 - Go 1.24+ - Wails v2 - Node.js 20 + pnpm ```bash # 安装 Wails CLI go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails@latest # 安装 pnpm npm install -g pnpm ``` ### 开发命令 ```bash # 安装依赖 make install # 启动开发模式（前端热重载） make dev # 构建生产版本 make build # 构建并安装到 /Applications （ macOS ） make build-install ``` 修改 Go 暴露给前端的方法后，执行 `wails generate module` 重新生成 JS 绑定。 ![]( https://open-cdn.tecmz.com/theme/apps/quotapanel/images/account-card.png?t=202609261508) ## 功能亮点 ### 新增账号管理 支持选择来源并填写 API Key 或发起浏览器登录，可自定义账号名称与备注，密钥默认脱敏展示并支持一键复制。 ### 浏览器登录 需要网页登录的订阅（ Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor ）通过独立 Chrome/Edge 窗口登录，登录会话持久保存，删除账号时一并清理其浏览器资料。 ### 卡片截图 一键将单张订阅卡片导出为 PNG ，方便分享或记录。 ### 定时刷新 默认每 5 分钟自动轮询一次，额度变化实时可见。同时也支持随时手动刷新单个或全部账号。 ### 托盘常驻 macOS 菜单栏/Windows 、Linux 系统托盘，快捷显示、重启、退出。关闭窗口行为可配置为「每次询问/直接退出/隐藏到后台」。 ### 多语言支持 简体中文/English 切换，界面与后端文档页配色集中到设计 token 管理，支持浅色/深色两套取值。 ![]( https://open-cdn.tecmz.com/theme/apps/quotapanel/images/setting.png?t=202609261508) ## 总结 QuotaPanel 是一款功能完善、设计优雅的 AI 订阅额度管理工具，采用 **Go + Wails + Vue3** 技术栈，支持 16 种 AI 订阅与 API 额度来源。 **核心优势**： - ✅ **开源免费**：采用 Apache-2.0 许可证，可自由使用、修改和商用 - ✅ **跨平台支持**：macOS 、Windows 、Linux 全覆盖 - ✅ **隐私保护**：所有数据本地存储，不上传云端 - ✅ **持续更新**：社区活跃，支持新增额度来源 **适用人群**： - AI 重度用户，需要管理多个平台的订阅额度 - 开发者，希望参与开源项目或自定义额度来源 - 技术爱好者，对 Go/Wails/Vue3 技术栈感兴趣 如果你也是 AI 重度用户，或者需要管理多个平台的订阅额度，不妨试试 QuotaPanel 。让它成为你开发工作流中不可或缺的一部分。 > ⭐ 如果这个项目对你有帮助，请在 [GitHub]( https://github.com/open-tecmz/quotapanel) / [Gitee]( https://gitee.com/open-tecmz/quotapanel) 上点亮 Star 支持开发者！

projects.summary: 这是一个给个人使用的自部署简历编辑器：选模板、填写经历，实时查看 A4 排版，再免费导出 PDF、PNG 或 JSON 备份。156 款模板无需解锁，简历数量不限；内容保存在自己的 SQLite 数据库。支持中文等七种界面语言，使用 Docker 或 Node.js 24+ 启动，适合愿意部署工具、希望自行保存简历数据的人。 亮点 模板和基础导出没有付费门槛：156 款模板全部开放，导出无水印。 不要求云数据库、Google 登录或支付配置；前端与 Node 服务端均使用 TypeScript，可作为完整自部署 Web 应用的学习样例。 支持实时预览、自动保存、撤销重做、模块排序、字体与配色调整。 AI 职位适配可选，需自备 API Key，服务商费用与限制自理；基础编辑、保存和导出不依赖 AI。 采用 MIT 协议，从本人维护的 JustCV 拆出自部署版本；付费托管服务与本开源版本分开。 当前一个安装实例只有一个共享工作空间，不提供多用户隔离。公网部署应按 README 更换默认账号并配置 HTTPS。 作者自荐；项目开发及投稿整理使用了 AI 辅助。与 xitanggg/open-resume 没有从属关系。

projects.title: 做了个用 Mac 控制家里所有安卓设备的小工具，手机之间也能互相控制，不走云端（Mac 免费下载 + 安卓内测招募）
projects.author: xxzhaoming
projects.summary: 家里抽屉里大概都躺着几台旧安卓：换下来的手机、孩子不用的平板、专门拿来跑某个 App 的备用机。每次想用其中一台，都得先找到它、充上电、解锁、在小屏幕上戳半天。 我想要的很简单：**坐在 Mac 前面，家里每一台安卓都在一个窗口里，点开就能看、能用。** 找了一圈，要么要登录账号、画面绕一圈云端，要么只能插线用。就自己做了一个，叫「统一控制」（ UnitCtrl ）。 ![Mac 上的统一控制]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhaoweijia1997/UnitCtrl/main/screenshots/mac-overview-zh-Hans.png) **Mac 上能做什么** - 家里的安卓手机、平板都在左边一列，插线或走 Wi‑Fi 都行，第一次设置好以后就不用线了 - 实时看画面，鼠标当手指用：点、拖、滚轮翻页；用 Mac 键盘往手机里打字，中文日文都行；手机的声音也能在 Mac 上听 - 应用管理、文件、截屏录屏，照片直接传进手机相册 - 每台设备今天亮屏多久、几点开的哪个 App 、存储还剩多少，一眼看到 **手机控制手机** 在一台手机上打开统一控制，家里其他装了它的设备会一张张列出来，点一下就能看它的屏幕、操作它。帮爸妈弄手机、够一下架子上的旧平板都方便。 ![手机上的设备列表]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhaoweijia1997/UnitCtrl/main/screenshots/android-devices-zh-CN.jpg) **几个我比较在意的地方** - **只在家里的网络里跑**：不要账号，不经过云端，我这边也没有任何后台，也就没有什么能被我收集 - **第一次连要对方点“允许”**：没点过允许的设备进不来，允许过的可以在设置里一键全忘掉 - **不用麦克风和摄像头**：传过去的声音只是 App 正在播放的声音 - **永远没有广告** - 老实说一句：局域网里的连接目前没有加密，请在自己信任的网络里用 **演示视频**（ 2 分钟，从打开到远程点一下）： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ALaN3L4hSbw **下载和内测** - **Mac 版**（免费，macOS 14 起，Apple 芯片和 Intel 都行）： https://github.com/zhaoweijia1997/UnitCtrl/releases 。还没做苹果公证，第一次打开请右键 → 打开。 - **安卓版**在 Google Play 封闭测试里（安卓 10 起）。个人开发者的新账号要凑够 12 人连续测 14 天才能正式上架，愿意帮忙的朋友： 1. 加入测试群组（点“加入群组”就行，不用审批）： https://groups.google.com/g/unitctrl-testers 2. 打开测试链接，点“成为测试人员”： https://play.google.com/apps/testing/app.unitctrl 3. 用同一个账号在 Play 里安装，装着别卸载，留 14 天 代码、界面、四种语言的翻译都是和 Claude 一起写的，我负责出主意和挑毛病。有 bug 、有想法，回帖或者写信 sublueai@gmail.com 都行。谢谢！

projects.title: Claude Code 账号被封怎么办？实战指南：封号原因、Persona 认证与网络排查
projects.author: EdwardParker
projects.summary: Claude Code 账号被封怎么办？实战指南：封号原因、Persona 认证与网络排查 更新日期：2026 年 10 月 适用于 Claude、Claude Code 账号暂停、Persona 身份核验、终端连接失败等常见问题。文中区分官方规则与社区经验，不把未经证实的“养号技巧”当成防封方法。 最近在 Claude Code 社区，能看到几类让人头疼的求助：有人正用 Claude Code 写项目，突然收到 Account suspended；有人登录时被要求完成 Persona 认证；还有人网页端明明正常，终端却频繁提示 Connection error，写到一半的任务反复中断。 这三种情况表面上都像是 Claude 出了问题，但原因可能完全不同。账号被停用，应该走官方复核；身份验证，应该按真实资料完成；网络连接失败，才需要逐层排查线路和客户端。 如果一上来就不断换节点、改时区、清缓存，很可能折腾半天也没找到真正的问题。 一、Claude 为什么会封号？先了解真正的风险来源 Anthropic 并没有公开一份所谓“封号风控评分表”，但其帮助中心明确列出了账号可能被停用的原因，包括： 违反使用政策或服务条款：例如反复触及被禁止的使用场景，或其他违反账号规则的行为。 从不支持的地区创建或使用账号：能打开 Claude 的网页，并不等于符合它的服务地区要求。 平台判断存在其他需要限制的行为：具体个案可能需要通过 Safeguards 申诉流程复核。 2026 年 10 月 8 日，Anthropic 发布新版 Usage Policy 说明，并进一步明确了 Supported Regions Policy 的适用范围：不仅涉及用户的实际所在地，也涉及企业的注册地、总部及相关控制关系。新版 Usage Policy 计划于 2026 年 11 月 12 日生效；地区资格不能简单理解为“出口 IP 在美国就可以”。 这里有个经常被误解的地方：地区限制不等于按中文语言或中国国籍一刀切。 是否有资格使用，必须对照官方当前政策与实际情况判断；换一个节点并不能改变真实所在地和账号主体的合规条件。 Anthropic 公布的 2026 年上半年透明度数据也说明，账号审查确实不是个别案例：官方记录了约 1,140 万个被封禁账号、39.8 万次申诉，以及约 4.2 万次被推翻的封禁决定。不过这些是平台总量，不能拿来推算“正常开发者的封号概率”。 二、先分清：账号封禁、Persona 验证和网络断流 | 你遇到的现象 | 更可能属于什么问题 | 优先处理方式 | |---|---|---| | Account suspended、Your account has been disabled | 账号限制 | 查看邮件和受限页面，按官方流程申诉 | | 登录时跳出 Persona，要求拍摄证件或人脸 | 身份核验 | 检查验证入口，按真实资料完成认证 | | Connection error、请求超时、终端掉线 | 网络或服务故障 | 查官方状态页、代理配置、证书及线路 | | Rate limit、额度耗尽、用量限制 | 产品使用限制 | 检查用量和计划规则，不要误判为封号 | 遇到异常，先保存完整错误信息、出现时间和对应操作。对于真正的账号限制，反复切换网络通常并不能解除封禁；对于普通连接超时，也不应该直接认定自己被风控。 三、为什么网络质量会影响 Claude Code 的使用体验？ Claude Code 与普通网页浏览有一个很大的区别：它往往涉及连续的交互、工具调用、较长的响应和多轮代码修改。一次网页加载失败，刷新一下可能就过去了；但写代码时突然断线，可能需要重新检查刚才的文件修改、终端输出和任务进度。 所以我判断网络服务是否适合开发工作，通常不会只看测速截图。真正需要观察的是： 晚高峰有没有明显抖动：平时能连，不代表高峰时段也稳定。 长时间连接会不会突然中断：几秒钟的测速与持续任务是两回事。 常用地区是否有可切换节点：某条线路发生故障时，至少方便排查和恢复普通网络工作。 客户端和分流规则是否成熟：浏览器能访问，不代表 PowerShell、Terminal 或其他开发工具也已正确配置。 这也是我会留意 AI 极客圈口碑极佳的 WgetCloud 的原因。选择这类高端线路的核心优势在于： IEPL 内网专线防断流：与走公网易受干扰的普通机场不同，WgetCloud 官网地址 采用物理专线跨境。这保证了在长文本对话、大规模代码生成或挂机时绝不断流，你的公网 IP 始终稳如磐石，从物理层杜绝了“IP 瞬移”导致的封号风险。 价格壁垒过滤污染源：相比廉价中转，WgetCloud 的准入门槛较高，严格限制带宽与在线设备数。这种高客单价天然隔离了羊毛党和恶意脚本，使得单节点 IP 纯净度极高，不会触发风控警报。 严密的底层防泄漏：支持原生接入 Clash / Surge，便于配置精细的路由分流规则，彻底防止 DNS 漏网暴露出国内真实的运营商 IP。 尤其当日常工作经常涉及 GitHub 仓库同步、海外技术文档和远程服务时，值得关注的是实际连接连续性，而不是宣传页上的峰值速度。 Windows + Clash Verge Rev：排查终端代理的一个实例 在符合 Anthropic 服务地区政策、且有权使用相应网络的前提下，如果网页端可用、Claude Code 终端持续报连接错误，可以按以下步骤排查： 第一步：检查 Claude 自身是否故障。 先打开 Claude Status，排除官方服务异常。 第二步：核对客户端的 HTTP/Mixed 端口。 Clash Verge Rev 的端口以软件实际设置为准；系统代理开启，也不代表每个终端程序都会自动继承。 第三步：检查 Claude Code 的代理环境变量。 例如，假设本机 HTTP 代理实际监听 127.0.0.1:7890，在 PowerShell 当前会话中可以检查或设置： powershell $env:HTTPPROXY = " $env:HTTPSPROXY = " 查看当前会话的设置 $env:HTTPPROXY $env:HTTPSPROXY 端口 7890 只是示例，不要照抄到与你的客户端设置不一致的环境中。上述设置只对当前 PowerShell 会话及其启动的子进程生效。Claude Code 官方支持 HTTP/HTTPS 代理环境变量，但不直接支持 SOCKS 代理；若使用了企业证书或网关，还需检查证书信任和网络放行要求。 第四步：判断是网络问题还是账号问题。 如果提示身份验证失败、账号停用或地区不支持，就应停止把它当成简单的代理端口问题。若只在特定网络、特定时段发生超时，则记录错误时间、测试其他获准的网络环境并检查客户端日志。 四、网上流传的“Claude 防封技巧”，哪些不能迷信？ 经常能看到这样的说法：注册后先“养号”几天、每天按美国人的作息提问、把 Windows 时区改成纽约、坚持同一个国家的 IP、换指纹浏览器就能提高账号权重。 这些都不能当成已被证实的规则。 Anthropic 没有公开证据表明，照着一套“人类行为模板”操作就能获得安全账号，也没有宣布“固定 IP 即可免封”。 更值得做的是这些基础工作： 1. 确认地区和账号资格：遵守官方 Supported Regions Policy，而不是只观察出口 IP 显示在哪个国家。 2. 保管好自己的账号：不要购买来路不明的成品号、共享登录凭据或把验证资料交给“代认证”服务。 3. 规范使用 Claude Code：通过官方支持的登录和服务方式使用；有团队协作、自动化或 API 需求时，按对应产品与授权规则部署。 4. 减少无意义的环境折腾：如果某个客户端本来就正常，不必为了所谓“风控玄学”频繁更改时区、设备标识或浏览器环境。 5. 保留自己的工作成果：项目放在 Git 仓库，重要配置、提示词和文档做好备份，避免账号异常导致工作被迫中断。 五、被要求 Persona 实名认证，应该怎么操作？ Persona 是 Anthropic 官方确认的身份验证合作伙伴。根据 Claude 帮助中心 2026 年 8 月 11 日发布的说明，部分个人或企业用户在访问特定能力、接受平台完整性检查或满足安全合规要求时，可能遇到身份核验。 出现 Persona 验证，并不自动意味着账号已经被封。 验证通过也不保证账号一定符合其他使用规则。 需要准备什么？ 个人用户通常需要： 本人有效的实体证件：政府签发、带照片、未过期且清晰完好。官方列举的常见类型包括护照、驾驶证或政府身份证件，最终以实际验证流程为准。 可以拍照的手机：验证过程中可能需要实时自拍或人脸核对。 正常的摄像头权限和清晰光线：避免证件反光、模糊、边缘被遮挡。 官方明确不接受截图、扫描件、证件照片的翻拍、电子证件或非政府签发的学生证等材料。至于能否接受某份具体证件，取决于核验页面及资格条件；不存在“拿中国护照就一定能过”“必须用外国证件”这样的通用结论。 如果 Persona 验证失败 先检查证件是否过期、照片是否清楚、摄像头权限是否正常，再按照页面提供的重试机会操作。次数用尽仍无法完成，应联系 Claude 官方帮助中心。 不建议采用网上所谓的“通关秘技”，例如拔掉 SIM 卡、关闭 GPS、强行禁用 WebRTC，或者使用指纹浏览器伪造环境。这些做法没有官方成功率依据，还可能造成新的兼容性和身份风险。更不要把证件、人脸视频或验证码交给声称可以“包过 Persona”的陌生人。 按照 Anthropic 的公开说明，证件与自拍照由 Persona 收集和保存，Anthropic 可以在有需要时通过 Persona 平台查看验证记录，但不自行复制存储这些影像；验证数据不用于训练模型。具体隐私细节以官方身份验证说明为准。 六、Claude 账号已经被封，如何提交申诉？ 如果登录页面明确显示账号已停用，官方给出的处理途径是 Safeguards 申诉： 1. 打开 claude.ai，登录被限制的原账号。 2. 在受限页面找到申诉表单，按要求填写。 3. 写清楚出现问题的时间、具体错误、实际使用场景和你认为需要复核的事实。 4. 提交后留意注册邮箱的回复；不要以重复注册、虚构身份等方式代替申诉。 英文说明可以简洁一些，不需要套用夸张的“保证解封话术”： text Subject: Request for Review of Claude Account Suspension Hello Anthropic Safeguards Team, My Claude account was suspended on [date]. I primarily use Claude / Claude Code for [your actual use case]. I would appreciate a review of this decision. Here are the relevant details: [error message, time, and factual context]. Please let me know if further information is needed. Thank you. 申诉不是百分百解封，但官方确实会推翻部分错误决定。 先前公布的申诉统计也说明，正常提供事实并请求复核是有意义的。 如需导出数据或删除账号，官方表示受限用户通常仍可在受限登录页面找到相应选项，但可导出内容可能受到限制。因此，代码和重要工作文档最好始终保存在自己可控的位置。 七、几个常见问题 Q：用了 VPN 或代理就一定会封 Claude 吗？ 不能这样下结论。社区个案无法证明“VPN 必封”。但使用代理同样不能改变实际地区资格，也无法保证平台接受当前访问环境。 Q：Claude Code 一直提示 Connection error，是不是账号被封了？ 不一定。先查 官方状态页，再核对终端代理、证书、网络日志；以账号受限页面和官方邮件判断是否真的封禁。 Q：Persona 要求提交护照，能否找别人代认证？ 不要。应当使用本人的真实、有效证件，且仅通过官方验证流程提交。找人代过会带来身份泄露和账号合规风险。 Q：选 IEPL、BGP 或更贵的线路，是否就能避免风控？ 不能。线路架构影响的是网络传输，账号权限和认证结果取决于平台规则。真正值得测试的是高峰稳定性、丢包、长连接和客户端兼容性。 写在最后 Claude Code 能显著提高开发效率，但也不必把“防封”想成需要伪装设备、模拟作息的神秘工程。 账号问题找官方申诉，身份问题走真实认证，网络问题查线路与客户端。 把问题分对类，比照着一串未经验证的技巧折腾更有效。长期依赖 AI 写代码的人，还应该把精力放在可靠的网络、可恢复的开发环境和自己掌握的代码资产上。

projects.summary: ServerlessInsight 是一个免费、开源的跨云 Serverless 应用管理框架，目前支持阿里云、腾讯云和火山引擎。通过 YAML 描述应用所需的云资源，再用统一的命令完成部署和管理，减少在不同云控制台中逐项配置资源、维护部署脚本的工作。 主要功能： 用 YAML 定义云函数、API 网关、对象存储、数据库及其关联，集中管理应用所需的基础设施。 采用基础设施即代码（IaC）的方式，配置文件随应用代码纳入 Git，方便记录修改、审查变更和团队协作。 分别管理开发、测试和生产环境，按配置重复执行部署。 部署前校验配置，预览将要创建、修改或删除的资源。 支持增量部署，并检测云上资源与配置之间的漂移。 在本地运行和调试函数，减少反复部署到云端测试的等待。 框架使用统一的配置模型处理不同云平台的部署细节，减少对厂商专属工具的依赖，降低跨云迁移的学习和配置成本。各云支持的资源类型有所区别，具体可查阅配置手册。 框架本身完全免费，可以通过本地命令行独立使用，不依赖 SaaS 平台。SaaS 平台仅提供扩展使用场景，可按需选择。 适合部署 API 服务、静态网站和定时任务，也适合需要维护多个云平台应用的个人开发者和团队。

projects.title: solace-vera-observability
projects.summary: Solace Vera sits between an AI's decision and its action. Before anything happens, the AI has to justify its reasoning. Every decision creates its own audit record with a unique fingerprint, so the AI can't go back and change its answers. All records are compiled into one full record over time. If the justification doesn't hold up, the action comes to a full stop and goes to a human for review. Open source.

projects.title: Show HN: Rouler – Steer Windows traffic per app or IP across multiple interfaces
projects.author: brndnbuilds
projects.summary: Hi HN, Rouler is "rules for your routes". It allows you to steer network traffic across multiple network interfaces on Windows. For example: - Run Tailscale, Mullvad and OpenVPN official clients simultaneously. - Use Rouler to send Slack via the OpenVPN connection, Chrome + an IP range via Tailscale and a torrent client via Mullvad. Rouler is VPN agnostic, so you can "split-tunnel" with anything that sets up a windows network interface. I'm an independent developer from Australia and have been working on Rouler for a bit over a year. It's been a challenging project to say the least, but I'm really happy with how it's turning out. I have spent a great deal of time building and throwing things away, starting over, belting the initial poc into something that I find intuitive... hopefully others do too! I've done all the testing, fixing and improving I can, so now it's open for public beta. I'd love to hear your feedback... and there are some specific points I'm interested in hearing about listed on the Rouler website. Please reply with any questions you might have. Thanks for reading! Brendan p.s. Rouler is "built in Rust" TM ;-) --- On AI (skip if you're sick of hearing about it): Since AI is the hot topic and people are naturally cautious about it, I'll add some quick notes about it, specifically about the driver development as that's the key thing to get right. The driver is hand written and every detail has been poured over many times over. I spent somewhere around 6-9 months manually building and testing just the driver, staring at Dbgview logs, wireshark logs, windows route tables, restarting VM's back to their snapshot and manually copying things across to start again. That's not always the most efficient way of doing things, but it's the way it had to be done. If I had tried to vibe code it Rouler simply wouldn't exist. I did try to lean on AI at times, but it constantly sent me in the wrong direction, told me things weren't possible, tried to take shortcuts and implement poor performing trade-offs. It also loved to hallucinate the windows api. Keep in mind this was around the Opus 4.1 - 4.6 days. Outside of the driver, in user mode land, AI has crept more and more into my workflow. I've had a lot of success utilising the latest models in the app in particular, and I purposefully separated the UI and core logic so I'm able to quickly iterate on the UI. I've also found AI very useful for scripting and refactoring. It has built some great scripts that would've taken me days or weeks to build and fine tune.

projects.title: Show HN: Daisy – macOS software KVM with native trackpad gestures
projects.author: tdewitt
projects.summary: I have three laptops on my desk most days. Each laptop is used for different work, that I need to keep separate. (Day job, advisory work, personal.) When I went looking for a software KVM, the only free one that correctly handled trackpad gestures was Apple's Universal Control but that requires using the same iCloud account on each system, which is a non starter. I had planned to just contribute to something else but the best option I found was intended to be a universal software KVM and had already rejected OS specific features. I get the thinking and don't begrudge the devs at all but I needed something that supports my workflow. Thus, Daisy (as in "daisy chain"). Daisy is a FOSS software KVM for macOS that doesn't need an iCloud account and handles gestures the way I want it to. You arrange the displays to match your physical desk, move the pointer across an edge, and control follows it to the next machine. Nothing leaves the local network (unless you want auto-updates) and there's encryption all the way around anyway. It turns out that getting the trackpad working is somewhat non trivial. macOS doesn't expose Spaces and Mission Control swipes through the public gesture events. They arrive as private DockControl events, which meant figuring out how to capture the gesture phases, progress, and velocity, transport them, and replay them on another Mac. There's a fair amount of undocumented macOS behavior involved, and I've documented what I figured out in the repo. Beyond gestures, the key things I wanted: - Capable of handling a large chain (8), with a layout tool that that makes it easy to arranges systems the way they exist on my desk - Copy/paste across machines for images, files, and folders - No accounts or other external dependencies - Keeping displays active across the whole chain when you're doing work, without violating the intent behind screen locking - No single machine acting as the control system that all peers must negotiate with for trust (the machine you're typing on is always the control system) It's not quite 1.0. Occasionally the layout UI loses track of a peer even though the connection is fine, input can sometimes get jerky, and I still need to beat on file transfers more. I use it daily, though, and it's reached the point where I find it genuinely useful. It currently requires Apple silicon and macOS 26 or later. I've tested on 26 and 27. Code, downloads, and the technical documentation are here: https://github.com/misfitdev/daisy I'd be particularly interested in hearing from anyone who's fought with macOS input events or tried to solve the same problem. And if you give Daisy a shot, I'd like to know what breaks. I'm also really happy about the security design and I'd love for people to poke holes in it. :)

projects.title: Show HN: Proxium – Self-hosted HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy with a web admin UI
projects.author: koldakov
projects.summary: With the team we are building a network management tool: switch upgrades, data collection/analytics, etc. With the write operations on production switches we've been requested to add an AAA flow so we have only 1 entry point for all microservices. For that reason we decided to add a proxy in the first place, so each request goes through the proxy, authenticates with External Authentication (the first A), then proceeds to the next step etc. First we thought about squid/envoy, but these proxies were declined by our devops as planned for the future. For sure we found a workaround, but then I thought why there are almost no proxies with UI/ACLs/limits/quotas/speed limits etc. So I decided to create my own solution that works out of the box with 1 simple command: docker run -d --name proxium -p 80:80 -p 8080:8080 -v proxium:/var/lib/proxium \ -e SUPERUSER_CREATE=true -e SUPERUSER_EMAIL=admin@example.com \ -e SUPERUSER_PASSWORD=change-me ikoldakov/proxium Then open http://localhost, log in, create a proxy account and use it: curl -x http://username:password@localhost:8080 https://ifconfig.me curl -x socks5h://username:password@localhost:8080 https://ifconfig.me Also, proxium supports https for the admin panel with self-signed certificates, let's encrypt certificates or your own uploaded ones. The proxy itself supports TLS too (self-signed, uploaded or imported from certbot). External auth is not supported yet, but it's next in the roadmap: an HTTP hook in nginx auth_request style first, then JWTs from your identity provider. SSO over OIDC for the admin panel is planned as well. I used AI for some parts of the code Feedback is welcome!

projects.title: Show HN: KiviDB, a faster Redis-compatible memory database and vector cache
projects.author: murtazayusuf

github.name: kividbio/kividb
github.description: A fast, multi-threaded Redis® and Valkey alternative written in Rust: drop-in compatible, with full-text and vector search built in

projects.summary: Hi all, So I have been working on this project KiviDB from February 2026. It started as a project for me to understand rust, having a product with no GC pauses, memory blow up after snapshots and getting OOM on running pods, and that was actually an issue I faced with Dragonfly. I wanted to have something picking the best of Rust, but also picking the best parts of other alternatives like Garnet and Dragonfly. I used AI a lot, but I was the one making the design decisions based on the tests that claude picked from my history of troubleshooting sessions as part of my job. KiviDB supports both RESP2 and RESP3 protocol. I had some founders credits on my AWS account which helped me with the infra, and running instances I could perform benchmark on. Its keyspace is sharded across threads, it is multi-threaded in nature, and performs best on Linux due to io_uring, I used the tokio_uring crate for this. It also has tokio fallback for other OS's. I hadn't open sourced it until recently as I felt it was not ready yet, the best way to learn it was to build a cloud managed service for it across all three widely used cloud providers i.e AWS, GCP and azure. Since I used to mainly work with cloud, I had some insights on what would be the best ways for the deployments, how to conduct failovers, manage SLAs, etc. And that's what I took help from claude to fast pace it. The website does look like AI slop but it works for now, given my limited resources, that's all I had. You may check it out at : https://kividb.io , I open sourced the core engine under AGPLv3, didn't want to have just source available, because that is available with other tools too. It supports apprx 98-99% of the redis 8.10 commands, few have issues and you can find them at https://github.com/kividbio/kividb/issues , contributors are welcome. Now the numbers, for the final benchmark, I used 2 c7gn.metal servers, in the same placement group in us-east1, and I used memtier-benchmark tool for this. The setting was : 10M keys, 100B each, 32 cores in use with both pipeline and un-pipelined runs. pipeline 16 GET: KiviDB 21.2M ops/sec vs Dragonfly 2.0 9.1M, Redis 8.10 2.4M, Redis Cluster 32 shards 4.7M When not pipelined, Dragonfly performed slightly better at 3.35M ops/sec vs kividb at 3.07M ops/sec. Memory per key was also slightly worse than dragonfly and almost same as Redis, 177B (kividb) vs 134B (dragonfly) vs 178B (redis). With vector ingestion times it was slower but when querying, it was faster than most alternatives at lower ef, however slower than dragonfly at high ef. Most of the technical details are mentioned here so you can check it out: https://kividb.io/benchmarks . easiest way to try it: docker run -d -p 6380:6380 kividb/kividb I am looking forward to building a community around this, provide better rust based tools, I am open to constructive criticism and value informed opinion. Thanks

projects.title: Show HN: Acyclic; Rapid agent swarms
projects.author: ramstar3000
projects.summary: Hi HN, we're the co-founders of Acyclic (YC F26). Acyclic runs any agentic workflow as a swarm. You give it a task and your project; it splits the work across many coding agents, each in its own sandbox, runs them in parallel, and merges what they produce into one patch or pull request. Our thesis: agentic workflows should be realtime, no matter how complex the task. The bottleneck should be human ideation and design, whilst building happens at the speed of thought. To bring this to you we make our agents recursively fork and speculative execute. This means that if an agent has 2 independent tasks to do, it will just split into 2 agents to solve both tasks quickly and merge back up the tree. Additionally, for sequential operations we have “speculative” agents which guess the next steps of the workflow as a pre-fetch step. To make this efficient we are solving the infrastructure bottlenecks. We are solving the memory, communication, routing and durable execution issues. This infra is open source at acyclic.dev/github, so check it out! To run your own swarm (check out acyclic.dev for a full guide) ``` npm install -g @acyclic-labs/cli acyclic swarm run --task <prompt> --dir <files_to_upload> ``` A good (non-coding) first task to try out: Do deep research into a person. “Do deep research into Jeff Goldblum“ You can view the results at acyclic.dev/dashboard or stream the results back to the cli using: ``` acyclic swarm pull <swarm-id> --apply ``` Check out some more research examples at acyclic.dev/evals, right now our biggest useful swarm is 236 agents for a code migration.

projects.author: DBAAZzz

github.name: open-wxa/wxa-runner
github.description: 在浏览器中用微信官方基础库运行小程序，支持 Chrome DevTools 调试与 Playwright E2E 测试

projects.summary: 我是项目作者。wxa-runner 是一个开源（MIT）命令行工具，可以在普通浏览器里运行微信小程序，用于本地调试和 E2E 自动化测试。 它不把小程序转成 H5，而是直接加载微信官方的基础库和编译器，自己只实现微信客户端的「原生层」：消息桥、页面栈、原生 API，以及导航栏、tabBar、弹窗这些原生界面。渲染、组件、setData、生命周期都由官方代码完成，行为和开发者工具一致。 在小程序目录（或 uni-app / Taro 编译出的 mp-weixin 目录）里一行启动： bash npx wxa-runner dev . --open 能做什么 AI Agent 可以直接操作：Claude Code、Codex 这类 Agent 最擅长的就是操作浏览器。小程序跑在浏览器里，它们用现成的浏览器能力就能点页面、看 DOM、读控制台和网络请求、写 Playwright 测试，不用为小程序额外配置开发者工具的自动化端口 用 Chrome DevTools 调试：打断点、看网络请求和 DOM，调用栈停在业务代码上，不会掉进基础库 Playwright 无头测试：直接在浏览器里跑 E2E，不用远程控制开发者工具，CI 里没装开发者工具也能跑 跳过登录：在 wxa.setup.ts 里预置 storage、mock 原生 API、拦截 wx.request，不用改业务代码 直接打开任意页面：地址加上 ?path=pages/detail/detail&id=1 即可 热更新：改页面的 wxml、js、wxss 不刷新页面，页面栈和全局状态都保留 测试写起来是这样： ts test('提交后跳转到结果页', async ({ miniProgram }) => { await miniProgram.mock('login', { code: 'testcode' }); await miniProgram.open('pages/form/form'); await miniProgram.current.locator('#submit').click(); await expect(miniProgram).toHavePath('pages/result/result'); await expect(miniProgram).toHavePageData({ status: 'ok' }); }); 当前边界 不替代开发者工具：预览、上传、真机调试仍然要用开发者工具 不支持蓝牙等设备能力，也不支持插件、分包异步化和 Worker 已在 uni-app（Vue 3）真实项目上验证，基础库验证过 2.32.3 到 3.8.8 之间的多个版本 欢迎试用。遇到跑不起来的小程序，请到 Issue 里反馈。

projects.summary: 想给喜欢的电影台词留个位置，最好能一起放上出处和画面，于是做了 ShotECHO 。 首页按北京时间每天换一句，背景图跟着切换，同一天刷新保持不变。往下只放 6 条精选，完整内容在「回响博物馆」里，能按分类、原文或译文找，也能随机看一句。当前初始内容有 26 条。 ![ShotECHO 真实界面]( https://alexjoker-blog.oss-cn-guangzhou.aliyuncs.com/%E6%8E%A8%E5%B9%BF/v2ex/01-overview.jpg) 托管条件是只能上传静态文件，所以用了原生 HTML / CSS / JavaScript 。解压后放进博客子目录就能用，服务器不需要 Node 或数据库； Node 只在本地维护和打包时使用。 相应的取舍是，投稿保存在访客当前浏览器的 IndexedDB ，收藏保存在本机，不同访客之间不会自动同步。可以把句子和图片一起导出，交给站长审核后再加入公共句库。它目前更适合个人收藏馆。 界面里的 IP 属地和收录时间是模拟展陈记录，页面已注明，不是真实用户数据。图片来源也有记录，公开展示时需要确认相应用途。预览地址： http://alexjoker.top/projects/ShotECHO/index.html

github.description: A persistent, Git-versioned map of your whole codebase and database schema that coding agents read before they touch anything. projects.summary: AOCI-CODE 将 AI 对软件项目的理解保存为可版本化的文本索引。模型基于源码，为文件和数据库表记录职责、关系、接口约定与重要约束；后续会话先读索引，再定位具体代码。通过本地 CLI 和 MCP 接入现有编程助手，适合接手已有项目、长期迭代和切换 Agent。项目采用 FSL-1.1-MIT，属于 Fair Source/source-available。 亮点 我们是项目团队，本次提交为自荐。 把系统理解保存在仓库里：索引记录对象职责和难以从目录结构直接看出的约束，由 Git 管理，可以审阅差异和回滚。 跨会话、跨 Agent 接手：索引与当前代码保持一致时，Codex、Claude Code、Cursor 等助手可以复用同一份项目认知，减少重新梳理系统的工作。 随开发增量维护：MCP 工作流发现受管对象的变化，由模型依据实际证据更新受影响的条目。 代码与数据库统一理解：可为数据库表结构建立独立索引，帮助 Agent 理解代码与数据之间的关系；不读取业务数据。 可供开发者学习的实现：项目用 Go 实现本地 CLI 和 MCP Server，源码展示了如何将模型撰写的认知索引纳入版本管理和变更维护流程。

projects.title: Show HN: Connecting Captions Local Private AI Interpreter
projects.author: chrisswimlee
projects.summary: Hi HN, I built Connecting Captions, a live captioning and translation overlay for macOS that runs entirely on-device. Nothing goes over the network: no API calls, no audio leaving your machine, and it keeps working offline. I wanted live translation I could use in meetings and conversations without worrying about connectivity, latency spikes, or sending sensitive audio to a third party. The technically interesting part is a low-latency, self-correcting pipeline for speech-to-text and translation. It has two modes: Sentence mode: buffers until a sentence boundary, then translates with full context. It’s more accurate, especially between languages with different word order. Streaming mode: translates word by word as speech arrives, trading grammatical accuracy for minimal delay. Current state: Platform: macOS Models: Whisper Latency: ~200 ms Languages: 25 Code: https://github.com/chrisswimlee/connectingCaptions I’d love feedback, especially on the self-correction approach and which use cases matter most to people.

projects.summary: 我在维护 [ZeninData]( https://zenindata.ai/)，这次分享的是 GridCraft 的独立浏览器托管入口和使用指南。 先说明归属：GridCraft 是 ArtCraft 团队及贡献者开发的开源表格编辑器，当前托管版本是 v0.7.0 ；我负责托管和站内指南。上游代码在 https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft 。 目前可以免登录打开本地 XLSX / CSV ，使用手动的公式、排序、筛选、格式和图表，再下载文件。工作簿在浏览器处理，本站没有表格上传或云端保存服务。域名里的 AI 是后续方向，自然语言 agent 仍在开发，当前体验使用手动控件。 对初次使用，建议先拿一个自己造的小文件检查： - 编号有没有丢前导零，日期和中文有没有变化； - 选几个已知结果的公式核对，再检查筛选和图表； - 下载后重新打开，确认内容仍在，再考虑处理正式文件。 GridCraft 还在 alpha ，复杂 Excel 文件可能丢失未支持的特性，VBA 不支持；完整的导入—编辑—下载—重开兼容性尚未完成验证。请保留原件，并在关标签页前下载更改。 站内目前有两份具体入口： - [打开 XLSX 的步骤]( https://zenindata.ai/guides/open-xlsx-online/) - [GridCraft 与 Excel 的适用范围和限制]( https://zenindata.ai/guides/gridcraft-vs-excel/) 免登录也不代表网页没有网络请求：官网使用 Google Analytics 统计使用情况，没有设置工作簿内容、单元格值和文件名的自定义分析事件。 如果试用遇到问题，欢迎描述浏览器版本、操作步骤和可公开的最小样例。希望收到的是实际文件工作流和指南是否清楚的反馈。 本文由 AI 辅助整理，产品定位和限制按当前官网核对。

projects.author: dmayle
projects.summary: I'm a software engineer from the east coast (who has lived in Boston, NY, the bay area, UK, France), and I built a task system called 3 & Done. It's the place you trust to store everything you need to do. It accepts voice input for rapid entry, as well as text (it stores the audio locally so you can listen to jog your memory) and emails you every morning with the three most important things for you to do that day, and why, based on what you've said about the task: deadlines, urgency, sitting too long. I've been at software engineering for about 44 years now... Grew up with it, which was unusual when I started, and I was always good about getting into the zone and doing things. The career started small, small company, then back office, the dot com startups, then smaller companies again after the bust, a non-profit, and eventually YouTube (Google at the time, but just barely) and Meta (just Facebook when I was there). When I hit the startups, and later big tech, it was no longer enough to just be an engineer, to have drive, to be good, you had to be organized, you had to follow through, get stuff done, and that's where the task systems started. Twenty-five over the years (and yes, I've actually counted), from Moleskine notebooks with Getting Things Done, evernote (remember evernote?), bug trackers, todoist, asana, google keep, among others. When I managed on the Facebook News Feed, I got into gantt charts (for me and my team), spreadsheets, OmniPlan... I remember apologizing to my director for being so disorganized (because I felt I was making a mess of it), and he told me that I was the most organized engineer he knew. That was because I was doing all of the work in the background, the trimming, the sorting, the reviews, but it was just so much work. Which was why I changed from system to system. Each time it built up, and I had to spend more time looking at things I couldn't or didn't get done, when I was rushed and couldn't put time into today's review, it would pile up, and then using it was so much work that I would start taking mini-notes, just emailing myself a few things to do the next day. That's actually the thesis of the app (but not where it started), that if I could just have a few things to do emailed to me each day, I could get it done. This app actually started when I described my previous startup failures into a Claude web session, and it repeated back to me what I had just said. My previous failures were because I spent too much time building the stuff I needed, and not building what I was supposed to be building. I decided that the app would email me three things to do every day (which matches best practices for attention), but that the day was always yours to decide. We won't overload you, but you can add more, if you're feeling up to it, or cut back, and we never shame and try our best not to nag (I often only finish two). If we get it wrong, you can tell us, and we'll re-rank it once a day, or you can set it manually, and if you do, we never override that choice. The web app is live, and native for both platforms is coming. In the meantime, on Android, you can use gestures to quick launch into the voice input so saving a task is only a gesture away (e.g. double-tap the back of a Pixel, double-press the power button on Motorola). Now let's talk about the dirty parts. I used AI to help me build this. Anthropic models mostly, and the brains of the app come from Anthropic models (I like the quality, I like the privacy, absolutely no training on customer data, and the stance of the company). This app is not some one-shot wonder where I asked frontier models to build a task system and then I put it on a server to show you. I have prompts for the various features (e.g. ranking, generating suggestions, task extractions), I have eval sets of task lists (not anyone's real tasks, but constructed from patterns in my tasks, or the tasks of testers who allowed me to fix the problems they were having), with the three I expect to come out. I store the eval outputs, and re-test whenever I add a new rule to a prompt, or whenever testing a new model version. The great thing about having this eval set is that it catches when I get it wrong. When I introspect a failed run, sometimes it's because I need to tune a prompt, but sometimes it's because I missed something in my own ranking. I did the same thing with my infrastructure as well, so this time, instead of setting up servers, and building login systems, and managing databases, I built on Vercel (git push to serving Next.js), Neon (hosted postgres). I started getting emails mailed to me by mid-June, but started getting usable suggestions on June 26, and I've been using it every morning since. I wanted it to be easy to get started, and easy to use, so the input handles mess (you can add multiple tasks in the same run-on sentence, and a friend who helped me test it just pasted his entire obsidian todo list in wholesale to get started). I wanted to make sure that anyone could try it out, so I built a trial feature that uses the real in-app ranking with a list of items you provide. If you want to try the service, there's a free 14-day trial (card required), and then it's $99/year or $9.99/month after that (plus sales tax). We warn you seven days before your card is charged and if you cancel, you keep access through the term (either the trial, or our last paid period). Online, through settings -> billing, no email, no call. I really hope you'll try it out. If you do, please tell me if we did a good job picking out your day. https://3anddoneapp.com/try

projects.title: 推荐免费工具：MiniToolDesk - 100% 浏览器本地运行、保护代码隐私的开发者工具箱
projects.author: Duxinghua
projects.summary: 工具名称 MiniToolDesk 访问地址 官网体验： 开源/主页： 为什么做这个工具？ 平时在写代码时，经常需要格式化 JSON、查时间戳、或者算个 MD5 哈希。但打开很多老牌在线工具站，往往扑面而来都是满屏闪烁的广告和弹窗，有些工具甚至会悄悄把敏感数据通过 POST 发送到第三方服务器处理。 特别是在大模型辅助编程时代，很多工程师会不自觉地把带有内部 API Key、JWT 凭证、数据库连接字符串的日志或代码直接喂给 ChatGPT / Claude，存在极大的企业数据泄露安全隐患。 因此我开发了 MiniToolDesk，核心理念只有一条：零服务端存储（Zero Server Storage），所有计算 100% 运行在用户本地浏览器内存中。 核心亮点与特色功能 1. AI 提示词敏感数据脱敏利器 (AI Prompt Sanitizer)： 自动检测并脱敏 OpenAI/Anthropic Key、JWT Token、数据库连接串、手机号和邮箱，替换为安全占位符； 支持本地双向解密还原：等 AI 返回生成的代码或分析结果后，在浏览器本地一键还原为真实密钥，防止企业机密泄露给大模型。 2. 纯前端 Web Crypto 硬件加速： SHA-256、SHA-512、MD5 计算与 AES 加解密完全调用现代浏览器原生 window.crypto.subtle API，断网离线状态下依然毫秒级响应，零字节网络传输。 3. 现代化代码生成矩阵： 支持 JSON 瞬间生成 Zod Schema、Go Struct、Python Pydantic、Rust Serde 以及 TypeScript Interface。 4. 桌面级纯净体验： 永久 0 广告、0 弹窗、无登录墙； 适配沉浸式暗黑/浅色毛玻璃界面，支持 PWA 离线安装及快捷键 Alt+M 侧边栏常驻。 支持平台 Web 端、Chrome / Edge 扩展插件、PWA（支持离线运行）。 欢迎阮老师及各位读者试用指正，希望能帮到经常跟代码打交道的开发者朋友们！

projects.title: Show HN: Gondwana, a code-first C#/.NET game engine with WebGL
projects.author: isthimius
projects.summary: Gondwana is a 2D/2.5D game engine for C#/.NET 8 that I’ve been building over the past 16 months, using SkiaSharp for rendering. I've spent my career creating web and distributed apps and that has influenced the engine's development, so it will feel very familiar to anyone with a similar background. The engine is deliberately code-first in its implementation but still includes visual authoring tools and a custom CLI. I started creating Gondwana to host my own RTS and SNES-style games, to offload the game ideas percolating in my brain. I wanted to focus more on creating gameplay systems and was less concerned with 3D graphics. The predictability and transparency of the old Win32/GDI era were the ideal for what I was shooting for, but I also wanted something faster and more portable than GDI32. To that end, I am not trying to emulate the bigger engines. Spot! became my primary dogfooding project that I’ve since pushed up to itch.io. Getting a game to that point really helped burn away the cruft that accumulates from trying to create something like this. I was able to get Spot! to render at a consistent 120 fps on my dev machine. I experienced the absolute ecstasy of getting WebGL to cooperate with the engine cycle. And I discovered that even if Gondwana is code-first, you don’t want to hand-code platformer levels, so I added Gondwana Studio to the repository. Studio uses the same file formats that are understood by the core engine. Asset handling was beefed up, UI widgets were added for things like game HUD elements and engine diagnostics, and I fleshed out the CI/release pipeline to keep it organized. As it stands currently, Gondwana supports GPU-backed OpenGL rendering with WinForms and Avalonia hosts, and a dedicated WebGL path with Blazor. Recently a good bit of effort has been put into optimizing the rendering hot-path, reducing contention between simulation and presentation, and into making the visual tooling easy to use by people other than just me. I even was able to get itch.io deployment down to a single command in the custom CLI. The engine is still actively evolving feature-wise, but the core rendering is pretty solid right now. I expect Gondwana will remain 2D/2.5D with parallax support, so I am not trying to supplant Unity, Godot, et al. Also worth noting, Gondwana intentionally does not have an explicit ECS framework built in, although one could absolutely work well with the engine if desired. The project is MIT licensed, the source is hosted on GitHub, the packages are on NuGet, and Spot! is playable in the browser at itch.io. I will include several links in the first comment under this. I’d love to see what other hobbyists or indie game devs think of the project. Feedback on usability, as well as praise and/or criticism of the architecture would be awesome.

projects.summary: btop is beautiful. But on my M-series Mac it can't tell me the one thing I actually want to know: what is the chip doing? No watts, no GPU, no per-core clocks. It also tells you what's wrong in plain words ("Busy: rustc using 9.1 cores", "Hot: fans at 80%") before you read a single graph. 10-second try, no load needed: brew install cloaky233/tap/siltop && siltop --demo Rust, MIT/Apache, no telemetry, no network unless you turn on update checks. projects.title: Show HN: RDST – A local agent that watches Postgres/MySQL for query regressions
projects.author: gvsg
projects.summary: We noticed during the course of many many years of DBA related work that fixes to database issues and queries are always reactive. An entire database can fall over extremely quickly when an unbounded query grows without warning. Traditionally, DBAs hear complaints of slowness and follow a methodical process: - manually browse pg_stats or other database related performance internal tables - see which queries are slowest - figure out what indexes are missing - figure out which indexes are actually bad and slowing down writes - painstakingly implement a fix In the age of cheap intelligence, we decided that there is no reason we can’t have an always-on agent that is designed to do this job for you. Databases need something or someone that is always watching with a massive amount of contextual understanding to be able to take quick actions. We’ve watched the alternative play out repeatedly. One of our users’s checkout page went from loading instantly to taking 11 seconds in a single night with no code change. How? Well somehow their order table grew by 40M rows because BI team had injected historical data and suddenly postgres started doing full table scans. Sometimes routine operations have unintended results and can easily destroy your database. We wanted to catch these kinds of regressions instantly. So we built RDST. RDST is a desktop agent that runs on your PC and connects to PostgreSQL / MYSQL (read only) and compares every query against its own performance every minute. Every expensive query is automatically EXPLAIN ANALYZED, stripped of PII and sent to U.S. based frontier or open model providers to analyze which indexes are missing, how the query could be rewritten, and provides the fix. We then run a classifier model (JEV) to decide if you should be notified (is this standard behavior for this particular query?), and the full history of the query performance is kept for years. RDST also keeps track of your entire database health in general, and recommends more fixes than simply bad queries. Since it runs locally we can keep the database credentials stored in your OS Keychain (RDST never keeps them in its own storage layer), and the connection goes straight to your database (using a jump host or SSH tunnel for private connections). You can read more about how we handle data especially as it pertains to LLM use here. https://readyset.io/docs/readyset-ai/rdst/desktop/privacy We really want feedback from the community from people running Postgres and MySQL in production. We are giving inference away completely for free. Just as a reminder, RDST will NOT run any updates or indexes against your database at this time. We are considering a fully autonomous auto-pilot mode in the future, but for now we are leaving the actual fixes in your hands. Let us know what you think!

projects.title: 做了半年无审查 AI 平台，记 4 个反直觉的工程坑（都有数据）
projects.author: largep
projects.summary: 我在做一个中文 AI 创作平台（对话、图片、视频、音频都有）。半年下来，最大的收获不是功能，而是一堆反直觉的坑。挑 4 个有数据的分享一下，对做 AI 应用的朋友可能有用。 ## 1. 「无审查」往往卡在托管商，不在模型本身 同一个图片编辑模型 **Seedream V5 Pro**，放在三家托管商上，用 40 条容易触发审核的编辑指令和同一张原图逐条测试（ 2026 年 8 月实测），被内容策略拒绝的比例分别是 **0%、12.5% 和 90%**。模型是同一个，差别全在托管商自己加的那一层审核：有的托管商在接口上根本没有提供关闭安全检查的开关，有的审核是概率性的，同一句话重试一次可能就过了。 所以挑「无审查」服务时，看名字没用，要看它实际跑在哪家，实测拒绝率是多少。 ## 2. DeepInfra 的 TTS 一过 15 秒就变成白噪声 长文本语音合成时，大约 60 秒的音频会在中段突然变成刺耳的白噪声。 抓包后发现，DeepInfra 在一个本该是裸 PCM 数据的流里，每 15 秒左右插入一行 45 字节的 SSE 心跳： ``` : ping - \r\n\r\n ``` PCM16 一个采样占 2 字节，而 45 是奇数。心跳一插进去，后面所有采样的字节都错位了一位，听起来就是白噪声。解决办法是在流里识别并剥掉这一行。如果你也在用 DeepInfra 的流式 TTS ，可以检查一下 300 字以上的长文本。 ## 3. Vercel 函数冻结，会吞掉「发出去就不管」的写入 计量日志和服务端埋点我们最初是 fire-and-forget 写的（`void fetch(...)`，不 await ）。后来发现，Vercel 的函数实例在响应发出后就会被冻结，没写完的 promise 会被挂起，直到下一个请求把实例唤醒才继续，而那时连接早已超时。 丢不丢取决于写入能不能在响应发出前的几毫秒内完成：复用热连接的数据库 INSERT 多半能活下来，要新建 TLS 连接的埋点请求则基本必丢。所以高峰期几乎看不出问题，低谷期和单次调用会稳定地丢数据，统计结果在半夜系统性偏低。 解决办法是用 `@vercel/functions` 的 `waitUntil` 把这些 promise 包起来，实例会等它们完成再冻结。修好之后，单次调用并静默 150 秒，计量和埋点也都能在响应后约 200ms 内落地。如果你在 Vercel 上做统计，发现半夜的数据总是少一截，可以查查这个。 ## 4. 长对话越长，回复末尾越容易出现乱码 我们统计了某个无审查模型回复末尾出现乱码的比例，发现它随上下文长度单调上升：上下文在 8k token 以内时约 0.01%，超过 48k 时到了 1.95%。短对话根本复现不出来，所以一开始一直以为是偶发故障。 更麻烦的是，一旦历史里出现过一次乱码，模型会照着抄下去。把 temperature 调到 0.7 之后，这种「被污染的历史」引发的乱码从 7/40 降到了 1/40 。所以先调采样参数，比去砍上下文更有效。 --- ## 最后说点题外话 这个项目从头到尾都是几乎我一个人在做。半年下来最大的感受是：一个人靠技术挣钱，养活自己是可以的。前提是选一个大厂不愿意做、或者做不好的方向，然后把那些脏活累活一件件干完。上面这些坑，没有一个是写功能时想得到的。 工具方面，最想夸两家。Vercel 是真好用：每个分支自动部署一个预览环境，合并到主干就上线，一个人也能保持很快的发布节奏，上面那个冻结的坑算是我交的学费。Cloudflare 是真良心：对象存储不收出口流量费，图片和视频这种大流量业务能省下一大笔钱，连域名邮箱都是免费转发的。 --- 平台叫 [思畅 AI]( https://sichang.xyz ），网页端可以免费试用，也有兼容 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 接口的 API ，可以直接接 Claude Code 。 --- 4 月 [发过一帖]( https://v2ex.com/t/1204769 )，当时大家提的意见都记下了。模型方面，默认模型已经换掉了。隐私方面，我们不再做「不存储」这种没法验证的承诺，改为隐私和便利并重：对话保存在账号下，手机、电脑多台设备可以同时使用，消息实时同步；传输全程 HTTPS, 数据库静态加密，数据按账号隔离；对话不用于训练任何模型，可以随时一键导出或删除。这里不是端到端加密，想要绝对的隐私，本地模型仍然是最好的选择。 欢迎拍砖。

projects.title: 第一个独立上线的 Web 站：用 3 天做了个 Rumpelstiltskin 踮脚舞 AI 视频生成器，记录一下踩过的坑
projects.author: komazhao
projects.summary: 做了很多年数据和产品，一直想自己从零上线一个能收钱的站。这次赶上一个梗，终于把第一个站发出去了，记录一下。 站点： https://rumpelstiltskinaivideo.app ## 它是干嘛的 10 月初 TikTok 和 X 上火了一个 AI 生成的片段：一个像 80 年代奇幻电影里的小矮人（ Rumpelstiltskin ），在堆满稻草的谷仓里，配着 Riff Raff 的 "Tip Toe Wing In My Jawwdinz" 踮脚跳舞。很多人想把自己放进这个片段里。 这个站做的就是这件事：上传一张照片，生成一段由你来跳舞的同款视频。 - 输入：1 张单人照片，不用写提示词 - 输出：约 11 秒、720p ，可选 16:9 （和原片同构图）或 9:16 （适合 TikTok/Reels ） - 文件：带原片配乐的 MP4 + 无声 GIF ，无水印 - 耗时：4 ～ 7 分钟，关掉页面也会继续生成 ## 技术栈 - 前端/全栈：TanStack Start - 部署：Cloudflare Workers + D1 + R2 ，Cron Trigger 补查超时任务 - 生成流程：Nano Banana 2 把照片转成彩铅风参考图 → 火山方舟 Seedance 2.0 mini 参考视频模式逐镜头重演原片 → 服务端用 Mediabunny 合入原片配乐 → 存 R2 - 支付：Waffo Pancake （ Merchant of Record ） ## 定价和成本 不做免费试用，单条 $4.99 ，3 条 $11.99 ，10 条 $29.99 ，一次性付费，不订阅，生成失败自动退积分。 没给免费额度，是因为每条都实打实烧 GPU ，新站扛不住白嫖流量。这个决定对不对，欢迎拍砖。 ## 踩过的坑 1. **照片太小直接被模型拒**：用户传了 260×626 的图，接口报 "invalid file"。后来在浏览器端先规整照片：短边小于 720 放大，长边超过 2048 缩小，极端长宽比补模糊边。 2. **用户关页面导致任务卡死**：提交模型后、写回任务 ID 前，请求被中断。改成 Workers 的 `waitUntil` 跑完后续步骤，Cron 兜底超时退款。 3. **PayPal 在日本一直登不上开发者后台**：最后换成 Waffo ，自己按文档手写 RSA 签名和 webhook 验签。 4. **Cloudflare 部署报 "compatibility date in the future"**：nitro 用本机日期写兼容日期，北京时间凌晨 Cloudflare 那边还是前一天。加 `TZ=UTC` 解决。 5. **Workers Builds 推送后一直"已加入队列"**：最后改成本地 wrangler 部署。 ## 关于 GEO 这次也在实践让 ChatGPT 这类 AI 搜索能收录、推荐我的站：写 llms.txt ，每个问题做一个答案页（第一句直接给答案、数字写死），加 FAQ/Article Schema ，接 IndexNow 和 Bing Webmaster 。效果怎么样还在观察，有结果了再来更新。 ## 求反馈 第一次独立上线，产品、定价、落地页、SEO 有什么问题都欢迎直说。也想听听大家做"热点梗站"的经验：热度一般能撑多久，热度过了之后怎么办？

projects.title: 【工具自荐】Video To Frames：在浏览器里把视频抽成图片，文件不上传
projects.author: crayon-nickee
projects.summary: 自荐一个我做的浏览器本地视频抽帧工具「Video To Frames」。 视频在你自己的设备上解码，不上传、不注册，抽出来的图片可以直接下载或分享。 在线版视频抽帧工具 浏览器访问（可免费使用）： 主要功能 七种抽帧方式：只取关键帧、按场景切换、每隔 N 秒、逐帧、固定张数、指定帧率、单帧。单帧可以在附近自动挑最清晰的一张。 在时间轴上拖选片段，或直接填写起止时间。导出前会先显示预计张数。 导出 PNG、JPG 或 WebP。可以打包成 ZIP、直接存进文件夹、复制单张，或拼成联系表。 文件名带帧号和时间码，方便对回原视频。课件录屏可以跳过重复画面，大致得到一页幻灯片一张图。 手机上可以把图片分享到相册。旁边还有视频转 GIF、视频转 MP3、HEIC 转 JPG、WebP 转 PNG，同样在浏览器里完成。 和其他视频抽帧工具的区别 文件不离开设备：用浏览器自己的解码器在本地处理，没有上传再下载这一步。打开开发者工具的网络面板，看不到视频被传走。 关键帧模式只读文件索引，不用把每一帧都解码，长视频通常几秒就能出结果。 同一次操作里覆盖封面挑选、课件转图片、逐帧动画、摄影测量和训练数据取样，不必为每种用途换一个工具。 免费、无水印、无需账号，也不限抽帧张数。特别长的 4K 视频受本机内存影响，可以只选一段，或按间隔抽。

projects.title: Show HN: Trustmux – Async tmux from your phone, now in Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora
projects.author: dustinkirkland
projects.summary: I'm Dustin Kirkland, author of Byobu. I recently flew to Australia and kept nudging my Claude, Codex, and Bash jobs along back home from somewhere over the Pacific, at 700ms of latency. That's what Trustmux is for: secure, asynchronous access to your tmux or Byobu sessions from your phone. I first posted this in June and since then there have been many point releases, lots of new features and testing, and a growing base of users. It's now packaged in Ubuntu 26.10, Debian, Fedora, and Chainguard OS. Why not SSH, Mosh, or Claude Mobile? - SSH/Mosh: a live, synchronous connection is brutal on a phone. Latency and WiFi-to-cellular handoffs make it laggy and fragile. - Claude Mobile: great for Claude, but I wanted access to whatever is running in my tmux session: shells, Claude, other code assistants. Trustmux is async by design. Connect, look, type a command, disconnect, with no fragile connection state to babysit. Security: TLS with real certificates, end to end. Uses Tailscale (cert provisioning via tailscale serve, no port forwarding) optionally, bind to your own network address, or bring your own or self-signed certs. Two security experts reviewed the design and I implemented their recommendations. More scrutiny is very welcome. Quick start: trustmux enable trustmux start trustmux pair # shows a QR code if qrencode is installed Open the URL on your phone, enter the 6-digit code, and add it to your home screen. It's a PWA, so there's no app store. Install: apt, dnf, pip install trustmux, or brew tap dustinkirkland/trustmux && brew install trustmux Under the hood: Python, libtmux, WebSockets, Tailscale, and no polling. The UI shell is cached for offline use. Part of Byobu, GPLv3. Trustmux isn't affiliated with the tmux project. https://trustmux.dev https://github.com/dustinkirkland/byobu https://pypi.org/project/trustmux/

projects.title: Show HN: Luksmith – Mount LUKS Ext4 Drives Natively in Finder on Apple Silicon
projects.author: baytizzel
projects.summary: I’ve recently moved over to macOS this summer and previously I heavily used Linux (still do as I have a homeserver running Arch and Omarchy Thinkpad for fun). I have a few LUKS Encrypted hard drives with photos I wanted on my Mac and then quickly realized that there’s no native way to open the drive. So I spent some time to make luksmith, essentially decrypting the luks drive, mounting the underlying EXT4 drive and using Apple’s Userland FSKit Library to make it appear in the finder window to make it as close to home on a Mac as I can (with journaling caveats because I can’t control which order writes happen in). It’s completely free to read and copy files from the drive if you try it out ‘brew install --cask betizzel/luksmith/luksmac’. And $9.99 one time purchase to unlock writing to the drive. No account needed, no telemetry shared back to me, no network connections made. Requires Apple Silicon + macOS 26. Full format support and limitations here: [ https://luksmith.app/#formats ]( https://luksmith.app/#formats ) available on the appstore: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/luksmith/id6806869711?mt=12 and the website: https://luksmith.app/#formats

projects.summary: **RoamDial —— 随机一站，听见世界。** 打开浏览器就能听全世界的直播电台，不用下载，也不用注册。 **按声音逛星图** 所有电台按地理位置铺成一张粒子星图。拖动地球，准星停在哪里就放哪里的台。按「下一站」就随机跳到地球另一端，听一听此刻那里在放什么。 **好不好听，先替你筛过** - 每周在服务器上把全部电台测一遍，只留真正能播的 https 台；随机池默认只挑码率 ≥128k 的 - 一个台有多条线路时，自动切到能播的那条；用户回报的坏台每天复查 - 各台原始音量能差到 30 dB，默认开着「音量统一」，换台不会突然吓一跳 **听到好歌能接着找** - 电台推送了曲名就直接显示；没推送的，点「识别这首歌」 - 能跟着唱的同步歌词，还能一键跳到网易云 / QQ 音乐 / Spotify / Apple Music 去听 - 电台和歌曲都能收藏，收藏列表可以拖动排序 **其他小功能** - 每个台都有自己的分享链接，发给朋友打开就是同一台 - 按流派、语言、国家、码率筛选 - 支持锁屏和耳机控制、睡眠定时，可以添加到手机主屏幕当 App 用 - 实验功能：浏览器本地跑 Whisper 出实时字幕 **怎么做出来的** 最早是在 Google AI Studio 里做出的一个原型，后来用 Claude Code 重写成完整产品，Codex 负责代码审查。前端是 React + three.js，后端是 Express + SQLite，部署在 Cloudflare 后面。上线后一直按 V2EX 网友的反馈在迭代，帖子里几百层楼的建议大部分都已经做进去了。

projects.title: Show HN: Petal, open-source CoScreen/ScreenHero finally free
projects.author: thedracle
projects.summary: Hi HN! I’m Jason Thomas, one of the founders of CoScreen. As some of you may know, Datadog sunset the CoScreen service on July 31st. Four of us from the original CoScreen team have spent the last couple months building a free and open source pair programming tool inspired by those that came before us: It’s called Petal ( https://github.com/kiruna-labs/petal ) Some history first, because when we started CoScreen we had hoped to break the sad and established pattern of this industry. Screenhero was an exceptional tool that a lot of us loved for pairing. Multiple cursors, low latency, you could click your partner’s editor, and just start typing. It felt like magic while we had it. Then Slack bought it in 2015, and shut down the standalone app in December 2017. When Till, Max, and I started CoScreen, we were aware of this history, and wanted to build an even more magical collaboration and screen sharing experience: the entire concept was “throw a window from your laptop up on someone else’s screen, and start collaborating with zero friction.” Datadog acquired us in 2022, and thus began the great adventure of adapting our real-time technology into Datadog products, while also continue developing CoScreen as a standalone tool from the Datadog ecosystem. Datadog invested in the product for years and we’re thankful for that. But CoScreen itself proved, like so many other screen sharing tool acquisitions, to be too tangential from the customer base and core mission. We instead built other communication features in Datadog, the integrations with other video platforms, and also its wildly successful MCP server. We weren't the only ones. Around was bought by Miro and shut down in March 2025. Multi (formerly Remotion) was acqui-hired by OpenAI in 2024 and shut down about a month later. It's nearly always the same story: a small team builds something hard that people love, a platform buys it for the team or the feature, and the standalone product doesn't survive the integration. So we decided firmly to do things differently this time. Petal is completely free and open source and we aren't monetizing it. If we lose interest or get hit by a bus, you can self-host it or fork it, and nobody can sunset it on you. Honestly it's a love letter to everyone in this community that supported us, believed in us, and to liberate collaborative screen sharing from this vicious cycle. We hope through this we can help foster a large and vibrant community around innovating in this product sector. What Petal does: shared windows show up as real windows on your desktop, movable and resizable, not tiles in a grid. Several people can share at once, everyone gets a labeled cursor, and you can click into any shared window to type and scroll. Rooms are persistent, so you click once to join "eng-sync" instead of passing links around. It runs on macOS and Windows (Linux is next, this time for real and you can help us!), plus a web app. Media goes over LiveKit. You can use our hosted instance with zero config, or point the app at your own LiveKit server with one docker-compose if you want the traffic to stay on your network or even use an entirely different video backend if you want to. The part that still feels strange to us: CoScreen took almost six years to build. The first version of Petal took under eight weeks, from scratch, with frontier models like Fable and Astra doing a lot of the work. Real-time video and window capture is some of the most unforgiving code we have ever written, so we didn't expect that. We will do a proper writeup on what worked and what didn't, and are happy to answer questions about it here. Till, Darren, Max and I will be in the thread.

projects.title: Show HN: Eevo – Consequential Decision Model
projects.author: ojalajuho
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Juho from Upright. I think we may have stumbled upon an interesting approach to AI alignment. The idea is as follows: 1. train a decision model to be really good at comparative sizing of consequences, expected value problems, and modelling overlap between different consequences 2. create a harness around that model that accepts a decision context, list of options, and identified consequences, then runs pairwise comparisons and overlap modelling for the consequences using the decision model in (1), and finally solves implied relative consequences "sizes" and finally EV (for different stakeholders) 3. Make AI agents running on general purpose LLMs use (2) to make better decisions. So the agent provides the context, options, and identifies the consequences, Eevo model just sizes them, models their overlap, and computes EV. In practice this seems to improve agent judgement a lot (in addition to adding lots of practical observability) It seems the (well-motivated) emphasis on instruction-following hurts model's performance on expected value tasks. The underlying decision model we trained beats Jev, Clef, MS decision-1 the model on OpenAI decisions API on economic rationality benchmarks like STEEP, expected value tasks, poker, and even Pacman (Jevman benchmark). I swear to you we did not Benchmaxx on Pacman Also it seems to be useful also for human decisions. Just getting other people's decisions presented to you in standard format with consequences listed and sized is just very pleasant. There are some testers though who think this is useful for improving everyone's judgement, except their own

projects.title: Show HN: TowerPanic – a family party game on a small FastAPI realtime engine
projects.author: ms209495
projects.summary: I want to show you the game I created recently and tell you whole the story/experience - including backend/latency/scalability. You can try it quickly without an account - I created game demo rooms (EU/US/JP) - links below - just be aware that anyone with a link can access join the game. Let's start with short description of the game itself: This is the TowerPanic game - you are standing on one of four towers, during each round some of towers crack, and some of these lean, and finally one of these colapse - you need to watch out to not be on the failing one. It's a multiplayer game for whole family. This can be also used as an icebreaking game - for people in any age. The game is safe for children - no violence, no strangers, no chat, no ads. Parent creates an account (free 14-day trial, then a paid pass) and starts the game - others join using a QR code or a link. Behind the game there is an interesting backend engine - I willdescribe it in a moment. Let's start with the history of this whole project: - I was playing with asyncio and fastapi - As an exercise I created a reliable chat application (multiple rooms, in each room each user can reliably broadcast a message to all other users) - I extracted communication to separate layer - creating network/application layer interfaces - 'reliable client' interface for client and 'state machine' interface for the service on server. - With these interfaces - I was able to create other service - an 'sgame' (simple game). With verified interfaces and created services (chat, sgame) I was able to ask AI to generate other tools/games - I was impressed by these results - the games/tools worked well - I deployed them on a remote server - I was surprised that the latency was very good - almost everything worked smoothly I tested the tools and games with my children and one of the game was really great. I decided to make this game public - I chose 'TowerPanic' name for it. I prepared an account/payment server for this game (as a separate FastAPI application). This was very good choice: - the game servers keep rooms only in memory - nothing persistent (rooms have expiration date) - the account server keeps all persistent data (it uses database) Because of this split I was able to figure out how to upgrade and scale frontend and backend independently - without significantly impacting users. I optimized the communication layer - so that it works in finite memory - only finite number of recent messages is kept, and I sent a full service snapshot (full state) to the lagging clients. The backend process (FastAPI/python) is limited by python GIL (only one core can be utilized) - to utilize all server cores I used HAProxy with consistent hashing to distribute rooms - so that users can be redirected to proper backend process. I tested how many rooms a single server can handle - it handles hundreds of active rooms in parallel with no significant latency drop. Before making it public I noticed that latency in other region of world might be higher and this could influence UX - I confirmed this using artificial delay on my remote server. I decided to deploy the application in three regions - EU, US, JP - to ensure low latency (below 150ms) in most of the world. The room is created in region closest to the user (best latency from the browser to backend). I needed also to prepare some legal documents (terms, privacy, refunds) - thanks to AI this was much easier. I'm a backend engineer, frontend/UI/UX were designed by me but code was generated by AI. To summerize all this work: - I'm happy that I was able to deliver complete game/complete product - I think the whole work took me about 20 evenings - I'm impressed that it was so short - I think this is because the technology I used is popular and all fits well - AI was great as a peer (to discuss the options for distributing the load, discuss were to locate servers, or discuss how auth/payments work under the hood, ... - based on this I could choose the best option) - AI was great for doing the non work which I'm doing ineffectively (frontend/UI/legal docs). The game is available at https://towerpanic.com/?ref=hn I will appreciate your comments/feedback: Product: - did you meet any obstacles to play ? - how smoothly it worked ? - please specify your location if it didn't work well - most important thing/things to improve ? - anything else ... Solution/Engineering: - one thing you will change in the architecture / approach ? - anything else ... If you don't want to register you can play directly using below links (2 rooms for each location, max 10 players in each room/board). projects.author: ryuukouki
projects.summary: 一份中文资料，讲清楚大模型的「拒答」是怎么训练出来的，以及怎么把它去掉： 原理：拒答由模型激活空间里一个固定的方向控制。abliteration（定向消融）把这个方向从权重里正交掉，模型就不再拒绝，而能力基本不受影响。 前沿实测：整理了 Anthropic 9 月报告的数据：GLM-5.3 经过处理后拒答率从 90% 以上降到 2%～3%，GPQA 得分不变，成本约 1,200～4,400 美元。也整理了这件事的另一面：7 月 Hugging Face 应对 AI agent 入侵时，前沿模型因为安全护栏拒绝做逆向分析，最后靠自己部署的开源 GLM 完成。 工具与部署：Heretic 等自动化工具怎么用，以及现成的去拒答权重、显存与量化怎么选。 平台横评：对话、图像、视频、语音各类平台的内容政策与价格，每条事实都附官方来源。 不收录越狱提示词，也不收录针对真实个人的换脸或声音克隆服务；文中列出了所有平台共同的红线，比如涉及未成年人的内容。 利益披露：维护者是思畅 AI 团队，思畅本身也在横评之列，优点缺点照写。

projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm the author. FACE is a single Go binary. You run `face` in the folder that holds your projects and it serves a page on 127.0.0.1. It speaks ACP (the Agent Client Protocol that Zed published) to the official CLI of the agent you already use: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Qwen Code or Antigravity, signed in with your own account. FACE has no model, no key and no agent loop of its own. Why I built it: a coding agent ships a feature in an afternoon, and three people and five sessions later nobody can answer "what is in flight, what did it cost, why was it decided this way". The answer I landed on is not a dashboard but a method where every decision and every delivery is a versioned file: a handful of docs written once, a queue with one line per delivery (docs/06), and one page per delivery (work/<slug>.md) that says what will be built and how it is proven before any code changes. The method is four slash commands the agent reads from one file (brainstorm, analyze, propose, apply); it works without FACE. FACE is the window: the queue becomes a five-lane board, a card opens into the page plus the live session, and the commit window shows exactly what the agent staged. The agent never commits or merges; you click. I built FACE itself with it, from the fourth week on. Before that the same method shipped a job marketplace in 89 one-page deliveries over 14 days, and a consulting project in 107 deliveries over 19 days. Install: `brew install jckodel/face/face`, `winget install JCKodel.FACE`, a `.deb`, or `curl -fsSL https://face.kodel.com.br/install.sh | sh`. macOS, Linux, Windows, arm64 and amd64. UI in en, pt, es, fr, de and zh-Hans. What is missing: single user and local only (a team mode with a server on your network is the next milestone); no editor (it shows code and diffs, your editor stays your editor); the source is not public yet. It will be visible under a fair source license when the paid tier for teams exists, and the free tier stays free. By itself FACE makes at most two requests, both off until you turn them on: a daily anonymous ping that counts machines and a daily version check. The page "What FACE sends" lists both URLs. Happy to answer anything about ACP, the adapters for Claude and Codex (they are not ACP native, so FACE wraps them), or the method.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】MastraWork：把 Agent 运行组织成任务的开源桌面 AI 工作台
projects.author: movclantian

github.name: movclantian/mastra-desktop
github.description: Local-first multi-agent coding workbench built on Electron, React and the Mastra framework. 本地优先的开源桌面 AI 工作台，基于 Mastra + Electron，把一次 Agent 运行组织成可暂停、可回溯、可交接的任务。

projects.summary: 项目：MastraWork | 平台：Windows / macOS / Linux | 许可：Apache-2.0 | 最新版本：v0.0.7 它是什么 一个本地优先的开源桌面 AI 工作台，底层是 Mastra 框架 + Electron。 它想解决的事情很具体：现在多数 AI 工具给你一段回答，事情就停在那儿；代码改到一半让它继续，它常常重新把文件读一遍，从接不上的地方往下编。前面聊过的上下文，像是没发生过。 MastraWork 的做法是把一次 Agent 运行组织成一个任务。任务落在具体的工作区里，长在线程上，每一步都留下痕迹。它能暂停，能回头检查，也能交给团队里的其他成员接着看。断掉之后不是从头再来，而是接着往下走。 它面向软件工程和知识工作：Agent、团队、工作区、终端、浏览器、MCP、技能和资料库收在同一个应用里，围着同一个任务转。 功能详解 🧭 工程任务 读取代码、全局搜索、编辑与 AST 修改、运行命令、查看差异、调用 LSP 都在里面。关键是读、写、执行分开授权，每一步都有记录，不是开一个大权限就全放开。 🛡️ 受控执行 计划、构建、复查三种模式，切的是「Agent 现在能碰什么」。人工询问和批准留在流程里，高风险动作停下来等人确认，不靠模型自觉。 👥 Agent 团队 主 Agent 可以带一群专家成员，支持委派、交接、并行、分支、循环和审批工作流。复杂任务拆给合适的人，而不是一个 Agent 硬扛。 🧩 开放扩展 模型 Provider、MCP Server、技能与插件、浏览器、资料库、记忆和网页检索，按需接入，不绑定任何一家模型服务。今天用这家，明天想换，配置改一下就行。 🖥️ 桌面集成 Electron 主进程、原生浏览器视图、PTY 终端、系统通知、凭据保险库。API Key、OAuth token 和 Cookie 由桌面主进程的凭据保险库保管。 📚 记忆与资料库 记忆跨会话保留；资料库统一收文档、表格和网页；用量、费用和历史数据随时可查。 一个任务是怎么走完的 一个任务从开工到验收，Agent 手里的权限是变的，分三个阶段： 1. 计划 —— 先把事情想清楚，读代码、查资料、出方案。 2. 构建 —— 方案定了再动手，改代码、跑命令、推进任务，每一步都留下记录，随时可以停下来回头看。 3. 复查 —— 对照差异和工作记录验收，高风险的操作在这一步需要人批准。 读、编辑、执行和外部工具在三阶段各有一套策略，图的入口在应用内设置里，实际安全性以服务端权限检查和测试记录为准。 技术栈 | 部分 | 选型 | | --- | --- | | 桌面外壳 | Electron 44、electron-vite、electron-builder | | 界面 | React 19、TypeScript、Tailwind CSS 4、CodeMirror 6、xterm | | Agent 框架 | Mastra 1.77（core、memory、rag、mcp、observability） | | 数据与检索 | libsql、DuckDB、fastembed 本地向量 | | 代码与文档 | Shiki 高亮、Mermaid、KaTeX、PDF 与 Office 解析 | | 工具链 | Biome、Knip、pnpm workspace | 快速开始 三个平台都有现成安装包，也可以从源码跑（需要 Node.js >=22.19.0 <23、pnpm 12.11.2）： sh corepack enable corepack prepare pnpm@12.11.2 --activate pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm dev 首次启动后配一个可用的模型 Provider、选一个工作区目录即可。需要网页检索、浏览器、MCP 或技能时，再按实际服务分别配置凭据。默认本地数据目录是 ~/.mastrawork，Mastra 服务跑在本机 4111 端口。 下载： 关于「本地优先」 需要说清楚一点：「本地优先」说的是桌面宿主、默认工作区和本地数据边界优先留在本机，不表示所有推理都在本地完成。模型推理走哪个服务由使用者自己配置，模型服务会收到你发过去的提示词和选定的上下文。 项目还在很早期（v0.0.7），用着顺手或者踩到坑，都欢迎来 Issues 说一声。

projects.author: j_leboulanger
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Ronan. I love the Nintendo DS but ran out of games that kept me hooked, so I tried porting the kind of game I play today: a factory game in the spirit of Factorio, on a 67 MHz ARM9 with 4 MB of RAM. I had never written code for the DS, and I built it with Claude Code. I wrote the specs, the design and the balancing, and Claude wrote most of the C. The post goes through how that worked, and through the technical parts I found the most fun: - a 2048x2048 world that is never stored: terrain is computed from (x, y), only the player's changes are kept in a hash table - night done by changing the 256-color palette instead of redrawing the screen - power grids and pipes computed per network with union-find (there is a small step-by-step animation in the post) - trains with schedules, block signals and pathfinding, plus redstone-like logic gates - a headless Mac build of the game with a text interface, so AI agents could play ~470 test sessions and even help balance the game You can download the ROM (English and French) and play it on a flashcart or in melonDS.

projects.title: Show HN: Hatoba, an open-source SSH client with an AI assistant and E2EE sync
projects.author: scarletkc

github.name: scarletkc/Hatoba
github.description: Open-source desktop SSH client with an AI assistant and end-to-end encrypted sync through your own Cloudflare account

projects.summary: I've used SSH tools for years and didn't really plan on building yet another SSH client, but I ended up building one the way I wanted. Hatoba is a desktop SSH client for Windows, Linux and macOS. It's written in Rust with Tauri 2 and MIT licensed. Each terminal has an AI assistant panel next to it. You describe the problem, and it reads the terminal screen, runs commands, types into the shell, and reads, edits and searches files on the host to find the cause and fix it. You can approve every command and edit it before it runs, let a model you pick approve the safe ones, or turn approval off. Files it changes show a diff you can undo. It works with any OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic API, local models included, and supports skills and MCP servers. Sync doesn't go through a server of mine. Hatoba deploys a Worker and a D1 database to your own Cloudflare account and syncs hosts, keys and AI conversations through them. The free plan usually covers personal use. Everything is encrypted on the device before it leaves. Keys are derived from your master password with Argon2id, every item is encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and the Worker only stores ciphertext plus the hashes it needs to sign you in. Someone who gets hold of the whole Cloudflare account still only gets ciphertext. Sync is optional, and everything works offline without it. The usual SSH client features are there too: groups, tags and fuzzy search, ~/.ssh/config import, ProxyJump and SOCKS5/HTTP proxies, an SFTP panel, local port forwarding, and a key vault that imports OpenSSH, PEM and PuTTY keys. There's also a dashboard showing CPU, memory, disk and network for every saved host, read over plain SSH with nothing installed on the servers. SSH is russh, the terminal is xterm.js with the WebGL renderer, and the UI is React. I develop on Windows, so it's Windows first, with a custom title bar that supports Snap Layouts and Mica, and working CJK input methods. The Linux packages and the macOS build get far less testing on real machines. The macOS build is Apple Silicon only and isn't notarized, so macOS blocks it on first launch until you allow it in Privacy & Security. Bug reports from Linux and Mac users would help the most. Website: https://hatoba.fog.moe Downloads: https://hatoba.fog.moe/download/

Permissions are intransparent and every provider ends up building the same integrations. We think there needs to be an independent tool that holds all connections to third party companies.
